Foreign key linking to procurement.catering_order. Business justification: Overbooking authorization changes affect expected passenger counts and thus catering requirements. Catering supervisors adjust meal orders based on overbooking limits to balance service levels and was

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Denied boarding compensation (voluntary and involuntary) is a direct cost tracked by cost center for financial reporting and DOT/regulatory compliance. Airlines monitor IDB costs against overbooking r
Reference to the revenue management analyst who applied the manual override. Populated only when rm_system_override_flag is True. Supports audit trail and accountability requirements.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — User Audit; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

description: Reference to the flight inventory record (specific flight departure date and flight number combination) to which this overbooking control applies. Links to the sellable inventory unit in Altéa Inventory.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Flight Inventory Object

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: Overbooking limits are constrained by passenger rights regulations (EU261, DOT Part 250). Overbooking control records must reference the regulatory requirement defining maximum oversale thresholds and

The approved percentage above physical cabin seat capacity that the revenue management system is authorized to sell. For example, a value of 10.00 means up to 10% more seats than physically available may be booked. Derived from historical no-show rates and spoilage risk models in Sabre AirVision Revenue Management.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Overbooking Authorization; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

description: The timestamp of the most recent real-time availability snapshot published to GDS and direct booking channels by Altéa Inventory. Indicates the currency of the current_booking_count and booking_limit values.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Real-Time Availability Distribution; IATA NDC

description: The average fare value in USD for bookings in this cabin on this flight, used as an input to the overbooking revenue optimization model. Enables the model to weigh the revenue benefit of additional bookings against the cost of denied boarding compensation.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Yield Optimization; IATA RP 1724

description: The computed maximum number of bookings permitted for this cabin on this flight, equal to physical seat capacity plus authorized oversale seats. This is the operative value consumed by Altéa Inventory and GDS availability responses to control seat sales.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Booking Limit; IATA Resolution 728

description: Historical cancellation rate (expressed as a decimal proportion) for this route, cabin, and season used as an actuarial input alongside the no-show rate in the overbooking model. Distinct from no-show rate as it captures pre-departure cancellations.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Cancellation Forecasting

description: Indicates whether this overbooking control applies to a codeshare inventory allocation rather than the operating carrier's own inventory. Codeshare overbooking controls may differ from mainline controls due to interline agreements and partner airline seat block commitments.
reference: IATA Resolution 788 — Codeshare; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Current lifecycle status of this overbooking control record. Active indicates the parameters are live and being applied by Altéa Inventory booking limit calculations. Suspended means overbooking is temporarily halted for this cabin. Overridden indicates a manual revenue management analyst override is in effect.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Booking Limit Management; IATA Resolution 830d

description: The date and time when this overbooking control record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Record Audit; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: The real-time count of confirmed bookings (PNRs) held against this cabin at the time of the last availability snapshot. Used to compute remaining availability and monitor oversale exposure.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Real-Time Availability Snapshot

description: Bitmask or string pattern (e.g., '1234567' where each digit represents Mon–Sun) indicating which days of the week this overbooking control applies to. Allows differentiated overbooking levels for weekday versus weekend departures.
reference: IATA SSIM — Day of Week Encoding

description: The maximum acceptable probability (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.0200 = 2%) that at least one passenger will be involuntarily denied boarding due to oversale. Balances revenue optimization against regulatory denied boarding compensation exposure under DOT 14 CFR Part 250 and IATA Resolution 830d.
reference: DOT 14 CFR Part 250; IATA Resolution 830d; EASA Regulation EC 261/2004

description: The scheduled departure date of the flight to which this overbooking control record applies. Combined with the flight inventory reference, uniquely identifies the specific flight departure instance.
The date from which this overbooking control record becomes operative. Supports scheduling of future overbooking parameter changes in advance of the departure date.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Effective Date Management

description: The date after which this overbooking control record is no longer operative. Null indicates the record remains active indefinitely until superseded. Supports time-bounded overbooking strategies.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Effective Date Management

description: Historical rate of passengers who arrive at the gate without a prior reservation (go-shows) for this route and cabin, expressed as a decimal proportion. Used in the overbooking model to account for demand that materialises at departure.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Go-Show Demand Modelling

description: Number of seats within the cabin that are reserved for confirmed group bookings and excluded from the overbooking calculation. Group bookings typically have lower no-show rates and are treated separately in the overbooking model.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Group Inventory Management; IATA Resolution 728

description: The input no-show rate (expressed as a decimal proportion, e.g., 0.0850 = 8.50%) derived from historical passenger behaviour for this route, cabin, and season. Used as the primary actuarial input to the overbooking authorization model in Sabre AirVision.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — No-Show Forecasting; IATA RP 1724

description: Estimated maximum financial exposure in USD for involuntary denied boarding (IDB) compensation if all oversold seats result in IDB events. Calculated based on max_oversale_seats and applicable DOT/IATA compensation rates. Used in revenue management risk assessment.
reference: DOT 14 CFR Part 250 — IDB Compensation Rates; IATA Resolution 830d

description: The date and time when a revenue management analyst last reviewed and confirmed or adjusted this overbooking control record. Supports governance workflows requiring periodic review of overbooking authorizations.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Review Workflow; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

description: The date and time when this overbooking control record was most recently modified. Tracks parameter changes by revenue management analysts or automated system recalculations.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Record Audit; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: The forecasted load factor (proportion of physical seats expected to be occupied at departure, expressed as a decimal e.g., 0.9200 = 92%) for this cabin on this flight. Input from Sabre AirVision demand forecasting, used to calibrate the overbooking level.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Demand Forecasting; IATA ASK/RPK Metrics

description: The absolute maximum number of seats above physical cabin capacity that may be sold, regardless of the authorized overbooking percentage. Acts as a hard cap to limit denied boarding exposure. Set by revenue management analysts in Altéa Inventory.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Booking Limit Cap; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

description: The scheduled date by which this overbooking control record must be reviewed by a revenue management analyst. Drives workflow queuing in Sabre AirVision to ensure timely recalibration before departure.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Review Scheduling

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes or context related to this overbooking control record, such as special event considerations, IROP recovery instructions, or coordination notes with ground handling teams.

Version identifier of the statistical overbooking model used to compute the authorized overbooking percentage for this record. Enables reproducibility, model governance, and comparison of model performance across versions in Sabre AirVision.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Model Versioning

description: Free-text justification provided by the revenue management analyst when rm_system_override_flag is True. Documents the business rationale for departing from the system-recommended overbooking level (e.g., special event, group booking, IROP recovery).
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Audit Trail; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

description: The actual number of physical seats available in the cabin for this flight departure, as configured in the aircraft fleet assignment. This is the baseline against which the overbooking percentage is applied.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Cabin Configuration; IATA SSIM

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code or regulatory jurisdiction code (e.g., USA, EU) identifying the regulatory regime governing denied boarding compensation obligations for this flight. Determines applicable DOT, EASA EC 261/2004, or national civil aviation authority rules.
reference: DOT 14 CFR Part 250; EASA Regulation EC 261/2004; ICAO Annex 9; ISO 3166-1

description: Indicates whether a revenue management analyst has manually overridden the system-calculated overbooking parameters. When True, the authorized_overbooking_pct and max_oversale_seats reflect analyst-entered values rather than the automated Sabre AirVision model output.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Manual Override Controls

description: IATA scheduling season code (e.g., S25 for Summer 2025, W24 for Winter 2024) during which this overbooking control is applicable. Overbooking parameters are typically calibrated per season based on seasonal demand and no-show patterns.

Identifies the originating system that created or last updated this overbooking control record. ALTEA = Amadeus Altéa Inventory automated calculation, SABRE_AV = Sabre AirVision Revenue Management model output, MANUAL = direct analyst entry.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory; Sabre AirVision Revenue Management

description: The maximum acceptable probability (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.0500 = 5%) that the flight departs with empty seats due to under-booking. Revenue management uses this threshold to calibrate the overbooking level against the risk of seat spoilage versus denied boarding.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Spoilage/Denied Boarding Trade-off Model

description: Number of seats held back from the overbooking pool to accommodate anticipated operational upgrades (e.g., elite frequent flyer upgrades, compensation upgrades). Reduces the effective booking limit to preserve upgrade capacity.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Upgrade Management; Oracle Loyalty Cloud FFP

description: The target number of passengers expected to accept voluntary denied boarding (VDB) compensation offers at the gate in the event of an oversale. Used in the overbooking model to offset the involuntary denied boarding risk.
reference: DOT 14 CFR Part 250 — Denied Boarding Compensation; IATA Resolution 830d

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the seasonal inventory plan record. Primary key for this entity in the Silver Layer lakehouse.

Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Strategic network planning allocates aircraft types to seasonal routes based on fleet composition, range capability, and seat capacity. Season inventory plans drive schedule filings and slot coordinat

Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Seasonal capacity plans (ASK, frequencies, aircraft deployment) are budgeted in financial planning cycles. Links planned inventory to revenue/cost budgets for variance analysis and board reporting. Co

Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign. Business justification: Seasonal marketing campaigns are planned against seasonal inventory plans (summer schedules, winter routes). Integrated commercial planning requires alignment between capacity deployment and marketing

Reference to the route master record for the origin-destination pair covered by this inventory plan. Enables route-level aggregation and network planning analysis.

Reference to the flight schedule record from which this seasonal inventory plan was derived. Links the inventory plan to the underlying schedule planning entity (route, frequency, and timing) as defined in the schedule planning system.

Foreign key linking to procurement.supply_contract. Business justification: Seasonal capacity plans drive long-term catering and ground service contracts. Procurement negotiates seasonal supply contracts based on planned flight programs. Essential for contract volume commitme

Name or employee identifier of the Revenue Management or Inventory Control authority who formally approved this seasonal inventory plan for activation. Supports audit trail and governance requirements.
reference: ICAO SMS (Safety Management System) Doc 9859; Internal Governance

description: The date on which this seasonal inventory plan was formally approved by the authorized Revenue Management or Inventory Control authority. Represents the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for the approval milestone.

Total number of bookings authorized for acceptance on this flight for the season, incorporating the overbooking strategy applied to total_planned_capacity. This is the effective sellable inventory ceiling used by the Passenger Service System.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Authorization Level; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

description: Number of seats planned in the Business Class cabin (including premium business variants such as Clipper Class, Club World) for this seasonal inventory plan. Zero if no Business Class cabin exists.
reference: IATA Resolution 728 — Cabin Class Definitions; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Number of seats within the total authorized capacity allocated to codeshare marketing partners for sale under their own flight numbers. Null or zero if codeshare_indicator is False.
reference: IATA Resolution 788 — Codeshare Agreements; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Flag indicating whether this inventory plan includes codeshare seat allocations (True) or is a purely operating-carrier plan (False). When True, codeshare partner allocations are governed by this plan.
reference: IATA Resolution 788 — Codeshare Agreements; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Timestamp when this seasonal inventory plan record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Serves as RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED for audit trail purposes.
reference: GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity; ISO 9001 — Quality Management

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which yield targets and revenue metrics for this inventory plan are denominated (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP').
reference: ISO 4217 — Currency Codes; IATA BSP (Billing and Settlement Plan)

description: IATA SSIM-standard days-of-week string indicating which days this flight operates within the season (e.g., '1234567' = daily, '135' = Mon/Wed/Fri). Uses IATA day numbering: 1=Monday through 7=Sunday.
reference: IATA SSIM Chapter 3 — Days of Operation

description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the arrival station of the flight covered by this inventory plan (e.g., 'JFK', 'CDG'). Used to identify the route destination.
Number of seats planned in the Economy Class cabin for this seasonal inventory plan. Typically the largest cabin and primary driver of load factor and yield management decisions.
reference: IATA Resolution 728 — Cabin Class Definitions; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Number of seats planned in the First Class cabin for this seasonal inventory plan. Zero if the aircraft configuration does not include a First Class cabin.
reference: IATA Resolution 728 — Cabin Class Definitions; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: IATA-format operating flight number (carrier designator + numeric suffix, e.g., 'AA101') for which this seasonal inventory plan is defined. Identifies the specific flight or flight series covered by this plan.
reference: IATA Resolution 762 — Flight Designators; ICAO Doc 8585

description: Flag indicating whether this flight's inventory is made available for sale through Global Distribution Systems (GDS) such as Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport (True) or is restricted to direct channels only (False).
reference: IATA Resolution 854 — GDS Distribution; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

business_glossary_term: IATA (International Air Transport Association) Season Code
description: IATA-standard season designator indicating the schedule period this plan covers. Format: S=Summer, W=Winter followed by 2-digit year (e.g., 'S24' for Summer 2024, 'W24' for Winter 2024). Aligns with IATA SSIM season definitions.

business_glossary_term: Initial Fare Class Bucket Authorization Levels
description: Serialized representation of the initial booking class (fare bucket) authorization levels at season open, as configured in Amadeus Altéa Inventory (e.g., 'Y:180,B:120,M:90,Q:60,V:30'). Defines the starting inventory allocation across RBD (Reservation Booking Designator) buckets before dynamic RM optimization. Confidential as it encodes pricing strategy. reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Bucket Authorization; IATA Resolution 728 — RBD

description: Flag indicating whether this flight and its inventory plan participates in interline ticketing agreements with other carriers (True) or is restricted to own-carrier ticketing only (False).
reference: IATA Resolution 780 — Interline Traffic Agreements; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this seasonal inventory plan record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Serves as RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED for change tracking and data lineage.
reference: GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity; ISO 9001 — Quality Management

description: The target load factor (percentage of seats filled) set by Revenue Management for this flight during the season, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 85.00 = 85%). Used as the baseline KPI against which actual load factor performance is measured. Confidential as it reflects commercial strategy.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; IATA Revenue Management Guidelines; DOT Form 41

description: Two-character IATA airline designator of the carrier marketing and selling seats on this flight. May differ from operating_carrier_code in codeshare arrangements. Null if same as operating carrier.
reference: IATA Resolution 788 — Codeshare Agreements; IATA Resolution 762

description: Minimum Connecting Time (MCT) in minutes applicable at the origin airport for this flight, as published for the season. Used by GDS and booking systems to validate connection feasibility for itinerary construction.
reference: IATA SSIM Chapter 6 — Minimum Connecting Times; IATA Resolution 743

description: Two-character IATA airline designator of the carrier actually operating the flight (e.g., 'AA', 'BA', 'LH'). Distinguishes the operating carrier from marketing carriers in codeshare arrangements.
reference: IATA Resolution 762 — Airline Designators; ICAO Doc 8585

description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the departure station of the flight covered by this inventory plan (e.g., 'LHR', 'JFK'). Used to identify the route origin.

The planned overbooking percentage applied to total capacity for this seasonal inventory plan, expressed as a percentage above 100% (e.g., 5.00 means 5% overbooking above physical capacity). Set by Revenue Management based on historical no-show and cancellation rates. Confidential as it reflects pricing strategy.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; DOT 14 CFR Part 250 — Oversales; IATA Revenue Management Guidelines

description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for this seasonal inventory plan, used in Amadeus Altéa Inventory and cross-system references (e.g., 'SIP-W24-LHR-JFK-Y'). Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this master resource.
Human-readable descriptive name for the seasonal inventory plan (e.g., 'Winter 2024 LHR-JFK Economy Inventory Plan'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for this master resource.

Current lifecycle state of the seasonal inventory plan. 'draft' = under construction; 'approved' = authorized for use; 'active' = currently governing live inventory; 'suspended' = temporarily halted; 'closed' = season ended; 'superseded' = replaced by a revised plan. Serves as LIFECYCLE_STATUS.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Plan Lifecycle; IATA SSIM

description: Classification of the inventory plan by its operational purpose. 'baseline' = initial seasonal plan; 'revised' = updated mid-season plan; 'codeshare' = plan governing codeshare inventory allocation; 'charter' = charter flight inventory; 'adhoc' = ad-hoc or supplemental plan. Serves as CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory; IATA Resolution 788 — Codeshare

description: Planned scheduled arrival time in local time at the destination airport, in HHMM format (e.g., '1145' for 11:45). Represents the published schedule time for the season as filed in IATA SSIM.
Planned scheduled departure time in local time at the origin airport, in HHMM format (e.g., '0830' for 08:30). Represents the published schedule time for the season as filed in IATA SSIM.
Number of seats planned in the Premium Economy cabin for this seasonal inventory plan. Zero if no Premium Economy cabin exists on the planned aircraft type.
reference: IATA Resolution 728 — Cabin Class Definitions; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: The identifier assigned to this inventory plan within the Sabre AirVision Revenue Management system. Used for cross-system traceability between the inventory plan in Altéa and the corresponding RM optimization model in Sabre AirVision.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: The last date of the IATA schedule season for which this inventory plan is effective. Corresponds to the IATA SSIM-defined season end date. Serves as EFFECTIVE_UNTIL.

The first date of the IATA schedule season for which this inventory plan is effective. Corresponds to the IATA SSIM-defined season start date (typically last Sunday of March for Summer, last Sunday of October for Winter). Serves as EFFECTIVE_FROM.

Total number of sellable seats planned for this flight for the season, across all cabins. Represents the principal quantitative capacity fact (MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE) for this inventory plan. Derived from aircraft configuration but stored here as the authoritative planned figure.
reference: IATA SSIM; Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Capacity Management

business_glossary_term: Planned Yield Target (Revenue per Revenue Passenger Kilometer)
description: The target yield (revenue per Revenue Passenger Kilometer — RPK) set by Revenue Management for this flight for the season, expressed in the operating currency per RPK. Used as the baseline revenue efficiency target. Confidential as it encodes pricing strategy.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; IATA Revenue Management Guidelines; DOT Form 41

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the commercial Origin-Destination (O&D) inventory segment record in the Amadeus Altéa Inventory system. Primary key for this entity.

Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Segment-level inventory control and nesting logic depend on aircraft type's seat capacity and cabin class distribution. GDS availability calculations and codeshare seat allocation require aircraft typ

Foreign key linking to inventory.cabin_class. Business justification: inventory_segment represents a commercial O&D segment sold in a specific cabin class. cabin_class is the reference master for cabin definitions. This FK links segment records to the cabin master. cabi
Reference to the underlying physical inventory leg (flight leg) from which this commercial segment derives its availability. A segment may span one or more legs in a connecting itinerary.
Reference to the scheduled flight record associated with this inventory segment, linking to the flight operations domain for operational context.

Total number of seats authorized for sale on this segment in the specified cabin and booking class, including any overbooking allowance approved by revenue management. This is the gross sellable inventory before netting sold seats.

Method used to control seat availability for this segment: 'leg_based' = availability derived from individual leg bucket counts; 'od_based' = availability controlled at the O&D segment level using virtual nesting; 'hybrid' = combination of leg and O&D controls.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Timestamp (UTC) at which the current availability figures (seats_sold, seats_available, load_factor) were last refreshed from the Amadeus Altéa Inventory system. Critical for GDS cache synchronization and real-time availability accuracy.

Single-letter IATA Reservation Booking Designator (RBD) representing the fare class bucket for this segment (e.g., Y, B, M, Q, V, W). Directly controls availability nesting and revenue management yield optimization in Sabre AirVision and Amadeus Altéa.

Number of seats allocated to the marketing carrier under a block-space codeshare agreement for this segment. Applicable only when codeshare_type = 'block_space'. Null for free-flow or non-codeshare segments.

Type of codeshare arrangement governing inventory allocation for this segment: 'free_flow' = marketing carrier draws from operating carrier's open inventory; 'block_space' = a fixed seat block is allocated to the marketing carrier; 'none' = not a codeshare segment.
Timestamp (UTC) when this inventory segment record was first created in the system, typically when the flight schedule was loaded into Amadeus Altéa Inventory for the season.

Scheduled departure date of the segment at the origin airport in local time (yyyy-MM-dd). Used as the primary date dimension for inventory availability queries and revenue management yield optimization.
Three-letter IATA airport code for the destination station of this commercial O&D segment as sold to the passenger. Defines the arrival point of the sellable unit.

IATA fare basis code identifying the specific fare product associated with this inventory segment (e.g., YLOWUS, BAPOW). Governs fare rules, restrictions, and the booking class bucket to which availability is mapped.
reference: IATA Resolution 728; IATA Fare Construction Rules

description: Availability status code published to Global Distribution Systems (GDS) such as Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport for this segment and booking class. Standard codes include numeric seat counts (0-9) or alpha codes (A=available, C=closed, L=waitlist) per IATA AIRIMP standards.
reference: IATA AIRIMP; IATA Resolution 787; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Number of seats currently held under group booking reservations for this segment. Group holds reduce available inventory and are subject to release deadlines managed by the group desk.

Indicates whether this inventory segment is eligible for interline ticketing agreements, allowing passengers to book connecting itineraries across multiple carriers on a single ticket. Governed by bilateral interline agreements and IATA BSP/ARC settlement rules.
reference: IATA Resolution 780; IATA BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

description: Current load factor for this inventory segment expressed as a percentage of physical cabin capacity that is sold or confirmed (seats_sold / physical_capacity * 100). Key performance indicator for revenue management and capacity planning. Note: this is a point-in-time snapshot value, not a computed aggregate.
reference: IATA Economics; DOT Form 41; Sabre AirVision Revenue Management

description: The IATA-format flight number as sold to passengers and published in GDS channels (e.g., AA1234). For codeshare segments, this is the marketing carrier's flight number, which may differ from the operating carrier's flight number.
reference: IATA Resolution 787; IATA Airline Coding Directory

description: Two-character IATA airline designator of the carrier that markets and sells this segment to passengers. For codeshare flights, this is the airline whose flight number appears on the ticket.
reference: IATA Airline Coding Directory; IATA Resolution 788

description: Minimum Connecting Time (MCT) in minutes required at the connecting airport for this segment to be valid in a connecting itinerary. Enforced during availability display and booking to prevent infeasible connections. Sourced from IATA SSIM MCT tables.

Hierarchical nesting level of this booking class within the cabin's availability nesting structure (e.g., 1=highest yield class, 10=lowest yield class). Governs through-availability rules: higher-level classes inherit availability from lower-level buckets per revenue management nesting policy.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; Amadeus Altéa Inventory; IATA Resolution 728

description: Two-character IATA airline designator of the carrier that physically operates the aircraft for this segment. Differs from marketing_carrier_code on codeshare flights.
Three-letter IATA airport code for the origin station of this commercial O&D segment as sold to the passenger. Defines the departure point of the sellable unit.

Maximum number of seats that may be sold beyond the physical cabin capacity for this segment, as authorized by revenue management overbooking controls. Expressed as an absolute seat count above physical capacity.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: IROP recovery costs (passenger compensation, rebooking, hotel vouchers) are tracked by cost center for financial impact analysis and operational performance reporting. Airlines monitor IROP cost expos

Foreign key linking to inventory.fare_class_bucket. Business justification: irop_reprotection records target a specific fare class bucket for reprotection. fare_class_bucket is the master entity for RBD buckets. This FK links reprotection records to the bucket master. fare_cl
Reference to the parent IROP event (e.g., cancellation, diversion, significant delay) that triggered this reprotection action. Links to the IROP event master record.
reference: Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops — IROP Event; IATA Irregular Operations Handbook

description: Reference to the original flight segment that was disrupted (cancelled, diverted, or significantly delayed), causing the need for passenger reprotection. Directly impacts inventory on the disrupted flight.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory; Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops

description: Date and time (UTC) when the Operations Control Center (OCC) formally authorized this reprotection action. Represents the principal business event time for this transaction.
reference: Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops — OCC Authorization; ICAO Annex 6 — Flight Operations

description: Indicates whether the recovery flight operates under a codeshare agreement. When true, inventory ring-fencing must be coordinated with the operating carrier's inventory system, adding complexity to the reprotection process.
reference: IATA Resolution 788 — Codeshare; Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Codeshare Inventory

description: Date and time (UTC) when this reprotection record was first created in the inventory system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.
reference: GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity; ISO 9001 — Records Management

description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the arrival airport of the disrupted flight (e.g., LAX, CDG). Denormalized for IROP reporting and route-level disruption analysis.
reference: IATA Airport Codes Standard; IATA Resolution 762

description: Scheduled departure date (local airport time) of the disrupted flight. Used for day-of-operations reporting and IROP timeline analysis.
IATA flight number of the disrupted flight (e.g., AA1234). Denormalized for operational reporting and IROP dashboards without requiring a join to the flight segment table.
reference: IATA Resolution 762 — Flight Numbering; Amadeus Altéa

description: Indicates whether passengers in this reprotection block are entitled to downgrade compensation (e.g., fare difference refund or EMD issuance) because they are being accommodated in a lower cabin class than originally booked.
reference: EU Regulation 261/2004 — Air Passenger Rights; DOT 14 CFR Part 250; IATA Resolution 735

business_glossary_term: Global Distribution System (GDS) Availability Updated Indicator
description: Indicates whether the real-time availability snapshot on the recovery flight has been updated and broadcast to GDS channels (e.g., Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) to reflect the ring-fenced seats. Critical for preventing oversell on the recovery flight.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — GDS Availability; IATA Resolution 788; SITA Airport Management Platform

description: Indicates whether this reprotection action involves rebooking passengers onto a flight operated by a different carrier under an interline agreement. Triggers BSP/ARC settlement and interline billing processes.
reference: IATA Resolution 735 — Interline Reprotection; IATA BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

description: Indicates whether the Revenue Management system has acknowledged and processed the inventory reduction on the recovery flight caused by this reprotection action. Ensures yield optimization models reflect the ring-fenced seats.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Availability Snapshot

description: Classification of the root cause of the IROP event that triggered reprotection. Drives downstream analytics on disruption patterns and recovery cost attribution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CANCELLATION|DIVERSION|SIGNIFICANT_DELAY|EQUIPMENT_SWAP|ATC_GROUND_STOP|WEATHER|CREW_SHORTAGE|SECURITY|MEDICAL|MECHANICAL — promote to reference product]
reference: IATA Irregular Operations Handbook; DOT 14 CFR Part 234; FAA Advisory Circular

description: Date and time (UTC) when this reprotection record was last modified. Tracks status changes, seat count adjustments, and authorization updates for audit purposes.
reference: GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity; ISO 9001 — Records Management

description: Reference to the Operations Control Center authorization record that approved this reprotection action. Ensures accountability and traceability of inventory ring-fencing decisions.
reference: Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops — OCC Authorization; ICAO Annex 6

description: Two-letter IATA airline designator code of the carrier actually operating the recovery flight. May differ from the marketing carrier in codeshare scenarios. Required for interline reprotection coordination.
reference: IATA Resolution 762 — Airline Designator Codes; IATA Interline Traffic Agreements

description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the departure airport of the disrupted flight (e.g., JFK, LHR). Denormalized for IROP reporting and passenger communication workflows.
reference: IATA Airport Codes Standard; IATA Resolution 762

description: Indicates whether the OCC applied an overbooking override to accommodate reprotected passengers beyond the recovery flight's standard authorized overbooking limit. Requires elevated authorization and triggers denied boarding risk monitoring.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Overbooking Controls; DOT 14 CFR Part 250; IATA Resolution 735

description: Total number of passengers displaced by the IROP event who are eligible for reprotection under this action. May exceed seats_ring_fenced if partial reprotection is applied.
reference: IATA Irregular Operations Handbook; DOT 14 CFR Part 250 — Denied Boarding Compensation

description: Number of distinct Passenger Name Records (PNRs) included in this reprotection action. Used to track the scope of the reprotection and reconcile against seats_ring_fenced.
reference: IATA Resolution 722 — PNR Standard; Amadeus Altéa Reservation

description: Priority tier assigned to this reprotection block, determining the order in which displaced passengers are accommodated on the recovery flight. ELITE: frequent flyer elite members; CONNECTING: passengers with onward connections at risk; MEDICAL: passengers with medical needs or SSR codes; UNACCOMPANIED_MINOR: UM passengers; STANDARD: general passengers.
reference: IATA Resolution 735; Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Priority Handling; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

description: Scheduled departure date (local airport time) of the recovery flight. Used to determine inventory impact window and reprotection timeline.
IATA flight number of the recovery (reprotection) flight on which seats are ring-fenced (e.g., AA1456). Denormalized for operational dashboards and GDS availability messaging.

Date and time (UTC) when unused ring-fenced seats were released back to general inventory. Populated when reprotection_status transitions to RELEASED or EXPIRED. Null if all seats were utilized or reprotection is still active.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Availability Management; IATA Resolution 735

description: Free-text operational notes entered by the OCC agent describing special circumstances, exceptions, or instructions related to this reprotection action (e.g., VIP handling, diplomatic passengers, group reprotection conditions).
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory; Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops — OCC Remarks

description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned by the Passenger Service System (PSS) to uniquely identify this reprotection action across operational systems and GDS channels. Used for cross-system traceability.

Current lifecycle state of the reprotection action. PENDING: awaiting OCC authorization; ACTIVE: seats ring-fenced and available for displaced passengers; CONFIRMED: passengers booked onto recovery flight; RELEASED: unused seats returned to general inventory; EXPIRED: reprotection window passed without use; CANCELLED: reprotection voided.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Availability Management; IATA Resolution 735

description: Classification of the reprotection strategy applied. SAME_DAY: recovery on same calendar day; NEXT_DAY: recovery on following day; MULTI_LEG: recovery requires multiple connecting flights; INTERLINE: recovery on partner carrier; UPGRADE: passenger accommodated in higher cabin; DOWNGRADE: passenger accommodated in lower cabin with compensation.
reference: IATA Resolution 735; DOT 14 CFR Part 250 — Denied Boarding; Amadeus Altéa Inventory

description: Date and time (UTC) when the reprotection inventory block expires. After this time, unused ring-fenced seats are released back to general inventory. Nullable if the window is open-ended until flight departure.
Date and time (UTC) when the reprotection inventory block was activated and seats became available for displaced passenger booking. Marks the start of the reprotection window.

Number of ring-fenced seats that were released back to general inventory after the reprotection window closed or the action was cancelled. Equals seats_ring_fenced minus seats_utilized when fully resolved.

Number of seats on the recovery flight that have been ring-fenced (blocked from general sale) for displaced passengers under this reprotection action. Directly reduces available inventory on the recovery flight.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Seat Availability Management; IATA Resolution 735

description: Number of ring-fenced seats that were actually used by displaced passengers. Compared against seats_ring_fenced to measure reprotection efficiency and inventory recovery.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory; IATA Irregular Operations Handbook

description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated this reprotection record. ALTEA: Amadeus Altéa Inventory PSS; NETLINE: Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops; SABRE: Sabre AirVision; MANUAL: manually entered by OCC agent. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.
reference: ISO 9001 — Data Provenance; Amadeus Altéa Inventory; Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops

description: Comma-separated list of IATA four-letter Special Service Request (SSR) codes applicable to passengers in this reprotection block (e.g., WCHR, UMNR, MEDA). Ensures special handling requirements are preserved during reprotection.
reference: IATA Resolution 831 — Special Service Requests (SSR); Amadeus Altéa Reservation

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each waitlist entry record in the Altéa Inventory waitlist processing engine. Primary key for this data product.

Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign_response. Business justification: Passengers may waitlist after responding to a campaign offer when inventory is sold out. Airlines track campaign-driven demand including waitlisted requests for demand forecasting. Essential for measu
Reference to the specific fare class booking class bucket (e.g., Y, B, M, Q) for which availability was closed and the waitlist entry was created. Drives revenue management yield optimization.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Booking Class Bucket; IATA Resolution 728

description: Foreign key linking to revenue.fare_class. Business justification: Waitlist entries specify the requested fare class (RBD) for clearance processing. Waitlist clearance algorithms prioritize by fare class yield, eligibility rules, and bucket authorization. Essential f
Reference to the specific flight inventory record (flight-date-cabin combination) for which this waitlist entry is held. Identifies the sellable inventory unit in Altéa Inventory.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Flight Inventory Object

description: Reference to the group booking record when the waitlist entry originates from a group overflow scenario (waitlist_reason = GROUP_OVERFLOW). Links the individual waitlist entry back to the parent group contract for group management reporting.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Reservation — Group Booking; IATA Resolution 728

description: Reference to the individual passenger profile associated with this waitlist entry. A single PNR may contain multiple passengers, each generating a separate waitlist entry.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Reservation — Passenger Profile; IATA Resolution 722

description: Reference to the Passenger Name Record (PNR) booking that is placed on the waitlist. Links the waitlist entry to the originating reservation in the Passenger Service System (PSS).
reference: Amadeus Altéa Reservation — PNR Object; IATA Resolution 722

description: Native waitlist sequence number assigned by the Amadeus Altéa Inventory waitlist processing engine. Serves as the business identifier for this waitlist entry within the Altéa system, used for reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and the source PSS.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Sequence; IATA Resolution 728

description: Single-letter IATA booking class (fare class) code within the requested cabin for which the waitlist entry was created (e.g., Y, B, M, H, Q, K, L, V, W, S, N, G). Directly maps to a revenue management fare class bucket in Altéa Inventory.
reference: IATA Resolution 728; Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Booking Class

description: IATA single-character cabin designator for the cabin class requested by the waitlisted passenger. F: First Class; C: Business Class; W: Premium Economy; Y: Economy. Determines the inventory pool from which clearance will be attempted.
reference: IATA Resolution 728; Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Cabin Configuration

description: Distribution channel through which the waitlist entry was created. GDS: Global Distribution System (e.g., Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport); NDC: IATA New Distribution Capability channel; DIRECT_WEB: airline direct website; MOBILE: airline mobile application; AIRPORT: airport check-in or gate agent; CALL_CENTER: reservations call center; INTERLINE: interline partner booking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GDS|NDC|DIRECT_WEB|MOBILE|AIRPORT|CALL_CENTER|INTERLINE — promote to reference product]

The actual booking class in which the waitlist entry was cleared and confirmed, which may differ from the originally requested booking class if the revenue management system cleared the passenger into a higher-availability bucket. Null until clearance occurs.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Clearance; IATA Resolution 728

description: Method by which the waitlist entry was cleared. AUTOMATIC: Altéa Inventory engine cleared automatically when bucket availability opened; MANUAL: airport or reservations agent manually cleared the entry; UPGRADE_PROCESSING: cleared as part of an upgrade processing run; IROP_REACCOMMODATION: cleared during Irregular Operations (IROP) reaccommodation workflow.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Clearance Method; IATA Resolution 728

description: Date and time (UTC) when the waitlist entry was successfully cleared and the seat confirmed. Null if the entry has not yet been cleared. Used to measure waitlist clearance latency and revenue recovery timing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Clearance Event; IATA Resolution 728

description: Date and time (UTC) when the waitlist entry was first created in the Altéa Inventory system. Serves as the business event timestamp for queue ordering and audit purposes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Creation Event; IATA Resolution 722

description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the arrival airport of the waitlisted flight segment (e.g., LAX, CDG, SIN). Used for route-level waitlist analysis and GDS availability messaging.
reference: IATA Airport Codes Standard; IATA Resolution 728

description: Date and time (UTC) at which the waitlist entry will automatically expire if not cleared, typically aligned with the flight departure time or a configurable pre-departure deadline set by revenue management policy. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Expiry Rules; IATA Resolution 728

description: IATA fare basis code associated with the waitlisted booking (e.g., YLOWUS, BAPUS21). Encodes the fare family, booking class, and applicable restrictions. Used by revenue management to validate clearance eligibility and by pricing to re-price upon confirmation.
reference: IATA Resolution 728; Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Fare Basis

description: Frequent Flyer Program (FFP) membership number of the waitlisted passenger. Used to apply loyalty-based priority rules and to credit miles upon clearance and travel. Classified as confidential PII as it is a unique personal identifier.
reference: Oracle Loyalty Cloud — Member Number; IATA Resolution 728; GDPR Article 4

description: Frequent Flyer Program (FFP) membership tier of the waitlisted passenger at the time of waitlist entry creation (e.g., NONE, SILVER, GOLD, PLATINUM, ELITE). Higher tiers receive elevated priority rank in the waitlist queue per revenue management policy.
reference: Oracle Loyalty Cloud — FFP Tier; IATA Resolution 728; DOT 14 CFR Part 253

description: Scheduled local departure date of the flight for which the waitlist entry is held. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Used for inventory snapshot reporting and waitlist aging analysis.
reference: IATA Resolution 728; Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Flight Date

description: IATA flight number (carrier designator + numeric suffix, e.g., AA101) for the flight on which the waitlist entry is held. Denormalized from the flight inventory record for operational reporting and GDS availability messaging.

Queue number assigned by the Global Distribution System (GDS) for this waitlist entry, used to route clearance notifications back to the originating travel agent or booking system. Null for direct-channel bookings.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Reservation — GDS Queue Management; IATA Resolution 722

description: Indicates whether the waitlist entry is associated with a codeshare flight operation where the marketing carrier differs from the operating carrier. True: codeshare booking; False: own-metal operation. Affects inventory allotment rules and clearance authority.
reference: IATA Resolution 788 (Codeshare); Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Codeshare Inventory

description: Two-character IATA airline designator of the carrier under whose flight number the ticket was sold (marketing carrier). For codeshare flights, this may differ from the operating carrier. Determines which inventory pool and allotment rules apply.

Indicates whether a clearance or status-change notification has been dispatched to the passenger or booking agent following a waitlist status transition. True: notification sent; False: notification pending or not applicable. Supports DOT consumer notification compliance.
reference: DOT 14 CFR Part 259 — Passenger Notification; IATA Resolution 722

description: Date and time (UTC) when the clearance or status-change notification was dispatched to the passenger or booking agent. Null if no notification has been sent. Used for DOT consumer protection compliance reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: DOT 14 CFR Part 259 — Passenger Notification; IATA Resolution 722

description: Two-character IATA airline designator of the carrier actually operating the flight (e.g., AA, BA, EK). Relevant for codeshare flights where the marketing carrier differs from the operating carrier.
reference: IATA Airline Designator Standard; ICAO Doc 8585

description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the departure airport of the waitlisted flight segment (e.g., JFK, LHR, DXB). Used for route-level waitlist analysis and GDS availability messaging.
reference: IATA Airport Codes Standard; IATA Resolution 728

description: Numeric rank of this waitlist entry within the queue for the same flight, cabin, and fare class bucket. Lower values indicate higher priority for clearance. Determined by Altéa Inventory based on booking time, fare paid, and frequent flyer tier.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Queue Management; IATA Resolution 728

description: Indicates whether a revenue management analyst manually overrode the standard Altéa Inventory waitlist clearance rules for this entry (e.g., to prioritise a high-value passenger or honour a corporate contract). True: manual override applied; False: standard automated rules applied.
reference: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Override Controls; IATA Resolution 728

description: Number of seats requested on the waitlist for this entry. For individual bookings this is typically 1; for group bookings this may be greater than 1. Determines the inventory units required for clearance.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Seat Request; IATA Resolution 728

description: Code identifying the operational system of record that originated this waitlist entry. Primarily ALTEA_INV (Amadeus Altéa Inventory) but may include GDS source codes for externally originated waitlist requests. Used for data lineage and reconciliation in the Silver layer.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — System Integration; IATA Resolution 728

description: Comma-separated list of IATA Special Service Request (SSR) codes associated with the waitlisted passenger (e.g., WCHR, VGML, UMNR). These SSRs must be honoured upon clearance and seat assignment. Stored as a denormalized string for operational reference.
reference: IATA Resolution 722 — SSR Codes; Amadeus Altéa Reservation — SSR

description: 13-digit IATA electronic ticket (e-ticket) number associated with the waitlisted booking segment. Follows the IATA 13-digit format (3-digit airline code + 10-digit serial). May be null if the ticket has not yet been issued at the time of waitlist creation.

Date and time (UTC) when the waitlist entry record was last modified in the source system, including status transitions, priority re-ranking, or clearance processing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Record Audit; ISO 8601

description: For upgrade-request waitlist entries, the cabin code of the originally booked cabin from which the passenger is requesting an upgrade (e.g., Y for Economy). Null for sold-out or group overflow waitlist reasons. Used by upgrade processing logic in Altéa Inventory.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Upgrade Processing; IATA Resolution 728

description: Business reason why the passenger or booking was placed on the waitlist rather than confirmed. SOLD_OUT: requested fare class bucket was closed; UPGRADE_REQUEST: passenger requested cabin upgrade pending availability; GROUP_OVERFLOW: group booking exceeded available allotment; OVERBOOKING_CONTROL: revenue management overbooking limit reached; CODESHARE_ALLOTMENT: codeshare partner inventory allocation exhausted.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Reason Codes; IATA Resolution 728

description: Current lifecycle status of the waitlist entry as managed by the Altéa Inventory waitlist processing engine. OPEN: actively queued awaiting availability; CLEARED: bucket opened and seat confirmed; CANCELLED: passenger or agent cancelled the waitlist request; EXPIRED: flight departed or deadline passed without clearance; REJECTED: system or revenue management rule prevented clearance.
reference: Amadeus Altéa Inventory — Waitlist Status Codes; IATA Resolution 728

Expiry date of the APU airworthiness certificate. APU must not be operated beyond this date without certificate renewal.
Certificate number issued by the aviation authority confirming the APU meets airworthiness standards and is approved for installation.
APU model designation as specified by the manufacturer (e.g., GTCP131-9A, APS3200).

description: Manufacturer part number identifying the APU model and configuration. Used for parts catalog and maintenance program applicability.

description: Unique serial number assigned by the APU manufacturer to this specific unit. Used for tracking maintenance history and airworthiness compliance.
Operating hours interval between borescope inspections as specified in the APU maintenance program.

Operating hours accumulated since the last major overhaul or shop visit. Reset to zero after overhaul. Used to determine next overhaul due.

description: Date when the APU was installed on the current aircraft. Used to calculate time-in-service and time-since-installation intervals.

Name or code of the Part-145 approved maintenance organization that performed the last APU overhaul.
Ownership and lease status of the APU. Indicates whether the APU is owned by the operator, leased from a lessor, on loan from another operator, or part of a pooling agreement.

description: Reference to the approved APU maintenance program document that defines all scheduled maintenance tasks and intervals for this APU model.
Name of the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the APU (e.g., Honeywell, Pratt & Whitney Canada).

Reference to the active MEL deferral if the APU is currently operating under a deferral. Empty if APU is fully serviceable.

description: Calendar date by which the next APU overhaul must be completed, based on the calendar interval limit.

description: Current functional state of the APU independent of airworthiness status. Indicates whether the APU can be started and operated.

description: Manufacturer-specified or operator-approved interval in operating hours between major overhauls. Defines when the next overhaul is due.
reference: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

description: Calendar time interval in months between major overhauls, whichever limit is reached first (hours, cycles, or months).
reference: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

description: Legal owner of the APU (airline, lessor, or leasing company). May differ from the aircraft operator.
reference: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

description: Timestamp when this APU status record was first created in the system.

description: Operating hours remaining until the next overhaul is due. Calculated as next_overhaul_due_hours minus total_apu_hours.
reference: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or special conditions related to the APU status and maintenance history.
reference: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

Reason for APU removal from the aircraft (e.g., scheduled overhaul, unscheduled failure, aircraft retirement, component upgrade).

Physical storage location or warehouse code where the APU is stored if removed from aircraft. Empty if currently installed.

Percentage of total traffic that is connecting through a hub, complementing O&D traffic to total 100% of market traffic mix.
Timestamp when this market assessment record was first created in the system.
Source system or data provider for the market intelligence used in this assessment (e.g., MIDT, IATA statistics, GDS data, internal BI, third-party market research).
Three-letter IATA airport code for the destination city in the O&D (Origin-Destination) market pair.
Year-over-year growth trend percentage for this market, indicating whether demand is growing, stable, or declining. Positive values indicate growth, negative indicate decline.
Boolean flag indicating whether interline ticketing agreements with other carriers could support this market without direct service.
Timestamp when this market assessment record was last modified or updated.
Percentage of total market traffic attributed to leisure travelers, complementing business traffic for total passenger segmentation.
Lifecycle stage classification of the market (emerging, growth, mature, declining) used for strategic network planning decisions.
Percentage of total traffic that is true O&D (Origin-Destination) point-to-point demand, as opposed to connecting traffic through a hub.
Three-letter IATA airport code for the origin city in the O&D (Origin-Destination) market pair.
Comma-separated list of month names or numbers representing peak travel demand periods for this market (e.g., 'June,July,August' or 'December').
Recommended aircraft type or family (e.g., A320, B737, B787) for operating this route based on demand, range, and economics.
Recommended number of weekly flight frequencies for this route based on the market assessment analysis, supporting schedule planning decisions.

Seasonality index representing demand variation across the year, where 1.00 is average, >1.00 is peak season, and <1.00 is off-peak season.
Slot availability status at the destination airport (available, constrained, unavailable), critical for slot-constrained airports under IATA WSG (Worldwide Slot Guidelines).
Slot availability status at the origin airport (available, constrained, unavailable), critical for slot-constrained airports under IATA WSG (Worldwide Slot Guidelines).
Total annual passenger volume (Pax) in the O&D market across all carriers, representing total market size for demand analysis.

business_glossary_term: VFR (Visiting Friends and Relatives) Traffic Percent

The percentage of scheduled flights that were cancelled. Calculated as (flights cancelled / flights scheduled) * 100. Key operational reliability metric.

The total number of scheduled flights that were cancelled on this route during the measurement period.
The total number of flights that were diverted to an alternate airport on this route during the measurement period.
The total number of flights that actually departed on this route during the measurement period. Excludes cancelled flights.
The total number of flights scheduled to operate on this route during the measurement period, as published in the airline schedule.

Overall qualitative assessment of route performance based on composite scoring of OTP, load factor, yield, and RASK against targets. Used for executive dashboards and network optimization prioritization.
The date and time when this route performance record was most recently updated. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
reference: ISO 8601 Timestamp Format, Internal Data Governance Policy

description: The percentage of available seats that were occupied by revenue passengers. Calculated as (passengers carried / available seats) * 100. Core capacity utilization metric.
The last date of the performance measurement period. Typically the last day of a calendar month or the end of a seasonal period.
The first date of the performance measurement period. Typically the first day of a calendar month or the start of a seasonal period.
The granularity of the performance measurement period. Monthly is most common for operational scorecards; seasonal aligns with IATA schedule seasons; custom supports ad-hoc analysis windows.
Free-text commentary on exceptional performance factors, IROP events, competitive actions, seasonal effects, or other context relevant to interpreting the performance metrics for this period.
The percentage of operated flights that arrived within 15 minutes of scheduled arrival time. Industry-standard KPI for route punctuality. Calculated as (on-time arrivals / flights operated) * 100.

description: The total number of revenue passengers transported on this route during the measurement period. Excludes non-revenue passengers (crew, deadheads, etc.).
Revenue per unit of capacity. Calculated as (total revenue / ASK). Key unit revenue metric for route profitability analysis. Expressed in revenue_currency_code per kilometer.
The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which total_revenue_amount is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
The total number of kilometers flown by revenue passengers on this route. Calculated as sum of (passengers on each flight * flight distance in km). Fundamental traffic volume metric.
reference: IATA Traffic Statistics, ICAO Statistical Reporting

description: The total operating cost allocated to this route during the measurement period, including direct costs (fuel, crew, airport charges) and allocated indirect costs (maintenance, overhead). Used for route profitability analysis.
The total passenger revenue generated on this route during the measurement period, including base fare, fuel surcharges, and ancillary revenue allocated to the route. Excludes cargo revenue.
Revenue per unit of traffic. Calculated as (total revenue / RPK). Measures pricing power and fare realization. Expressed in revenue_currency_code per kilometer.

Reference code for the bilateral air service agreement governing this city pair (e.g., US-UK Open Skies, US-Japan bilateral). Determines traffic rights, capacity limits, and operational freedoms.

Market competition classification based on number of carriers serving the city pair: monopoly (single carrier), duopoly (two carriers), oligopoly (3-5 carriers), highly_competitive (6+ carriers).

Three-letter IATA airport code representing the destination point of the city pair (e.g., JFK, LAX, LHR).
Three-letter IATA city code for the destination metropolitan area. May differ from airport code when multiple airports serve one city (e.g., LON for LHR/LGW/STN).

Indicates whether the city pair is defined as one-way (origin to destination only) or bidirectional (both directions treated as same market for analysis).

Categorical classification of route length: short_haul (<1500km), medium_haul (1500-4000km), long_haul (4000-8000km), ultra_long_haul (>8000km). Used for fleet assignment, crew planning, and market segmentation.
Date when this city pair definition became effective in the airline's route network. Used for historical analysis and schedule planning.
Date when this city pair definition ceased to be effective (nullable for currently active city pairs). Used for historical analysis and route discontinuation tracking.

description: Indicates whether ETOPS certification is required for twin-engine aircraft operations on this city pair due to extended overwater or remote routing beyond 60 minutes single-engine diversion time.
Shortest distance between origin and destination airports measured along the surface of the Earth (great circle route), expressed in kilometers. Used for ASK and RPK calculations.
Shortest distance between origin and destination airports measured along the surface of the Earth (great circle route), expressed in statute miles. Used for mileage accrual in FFP programs.
Network topology classification indicating whether the city pair connects two hubs, a hub to a spoke, two spokes, or operates as a point-to-point route outside the hub network.
Indicates whether this city pair is eligible for interline ticketing agreements with partner carriers, allowing through-ticketing and baggage transfer.
Timestamp when this city pair record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

Classification of the city pair market type: domestic (within same country), international (between different countries), or transborder (specific cross-border markets with special regulatory treatment, e.g., US-Canada).
Lifecycle stage of the city pair market: emerging (new route, low traffic), growth (increasing demand), mature (stable established market), declining (reducing demand).

Minimum time in minutes required for passenger connections at the origin or destination hub when this city pair is part of a connecting itinerary. Used for schedule feasibility and inventory availability.
Three-letter IATA city code for the origin metropolitan area. May differ from airport code when multiple airports serve one city (e.g., NYC for JFK/LGA/EWR).
Three-letter ISO country code for the origin country (e.g., USA, GBR, FRA).
IATA Traffic Conference region for the origin (TC1=Americas, TC2=Europe/Africa/Middle East, TC3=Asia/Pacific). Used for fare construction and bilateral agreement classification.

Actual flown distance based on typical flight routing including airways, ATC routing, and operational constraints. May differ from great circle distance due to airspace restrictions, weather routing, or operational procedures.

Typical seasonal operating pattern for this city pair: year_round (continuous service), summer_only (IATA summer season), winter_only (IATA winter season), peak_season (high-demand periods), shoulder_season (transitional periods).
Indicates whether either the origin or destination airport is slot-controlled under IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (Level 3 airport), requiring allocated takeoff and landing slots.

Time difference in hours between origin and destination time zones. Positive values indicate destination is ahead; negative values indicate destination is behind. Used for schedule planning and passenger communication.

Average scheduled block time (gate-to-gate time) in minutes for flights operating this city pair, including taxi time. Used for crew scheduling, aircraft utilization planning, and schedule design.

Reference to the codeshare agreement governing this flight number assignment. Null for operating flights. Links to the bilateral codeshare contract between marketing and operating carriers.

Reference to the airport slot allocation record for constrained airports. Links to the assigned takeoff/landing time window granted by the airport coordinator or Air Traffic Control (ATC).
Reference code or identifier for the bilateral air service agreement between countries that authorizes this route. Governs traffic rights and frequencies under international aviation treaties.
