business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Carrier Code
description: Two-character IATA airline designator code identifying the carrier (e.g., AA for American Airlines, BA for British Airways). Used as prefix for flight numbers.
Timestamp when this flight number record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight's destination/arrival airport (e.g., LAX, CDG, SIN).
Directional classification of the flight within the route network: outbound (departing from hub), inbound (arriving at hub), circular (multi-leg routing returning to origin).
Great circle distance in kilometers between origin and destination airports. Used for Revenue Passenger Kilometer (RPK) and Available Seat Kilometer (ASK) calculations.
Date when this flight number assignment becomes active and valid for scheduling and reservations. Start of the flight number's lifecycle.
Date when this flight number assignment expires or is discontinued. Null indicates an open-ended assignment. End of the flight number's lifecycle.

business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certified Indicator
description: Flag indicating whether this flight operates under Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) certification for extended overwater or remote area operations (true) or standard operations (false).
Numeric flight number designator (1-4 digits) with optional single-letter suffix. Combined with carrier code forms the complete flight identifier (e.g., 1234, 567A).

Current lifecycle status of the flight number: active (in operational use), inactive (temporarily not scheduled), suspended (operationally blocked), pending (approved but not yet active), retired (permanently discontinued).

Classification of the flight number based on operational arrangement: operating (airline operates the flight), codeshare (marketing carrier sells seats on another carrier's flight), wetlease (aircraft leased with crew), drylease (aircraft leased without crew), blocked (reserved but not in active use).
Scheduled airborne flight time in minutes from wheels-off to wheels-on. Excludes ground taxi time.
Seven-character string indicating days of operation (1=operates, 0=does not operate) in sequence Monday through Sunday (e.g., 1111100 = Monday-Friday only, 0000011 = weekends only).
Complete flight number including carrier code and numeric designator (e.g., AA1234, BA567A). This is the externally-known business identifier displayed to passengers and used in reservations.

Flag indicating whether this flight number is distributed through Global Distribution Systems (GDS) such as Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport for travel agency bookings (true) or restricted to direct channels (false).

business_glossary_term: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Carrier Code
description: Three-character ICAO airline designator code for the carrier (e.g., AAL for American Airlines, BAW for British Airways). Used in flight plans and air traffic control communications.
Flag indicating whether this flight number is eligible for interline ticketing agreements with partner carriers (true) or restricted to online bookings only (false).
Timestamp when this flight number record was last updated. Audit trail for change tracking and data quality monitoring.
IATA code of the airline that markets and sells the flight. For codeshare flights, this is the carrier whose flight number is displayed. For operating flights, this matches the carrier_code.
User identifier or system account that last modified this flight number record. Supports audit trail and accountability for schedule changes.
Flag indicating whether this flight serves a hub airport in the carrier's hub-and-spoke network topology (true) or is a point-to-point spoke route (false).
Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight's origin/departure airport (e.g., JFK, LHR, DXB).

Internal priority ranking for this flight number within the carrier's network. Lower numbers indicate higher priority for resource allocation, slot protection, and operational recovery during Irregular Operations (IROP).

Free-text field for operational notes, special handling instructions, or additional context about this flight number assignment. May include codeshare display rules, seasonal variations, or historical notes.
Revenue management classification code used for yield optimization and inventory control strategies. Aligns with Sabre AirVision Revenue Management system classifications.
IATA season code indicating the scheduling season (e.g., S24 for Summer 2024, W24 for Winter 2024/2025). Format: S/W followed by two-digit year.
Flag indicating whether this flight number is assigned on a seasonal basis (true) or year-round (false). Seasonal flights typically operate during peak travel periods (summer, winter holidays).

Type of service provided by the flight: passenger (revenue passenger service), cargo (freight only), combi (mixed passenger and cargo), ferry (non-revenue aircraft repositioning), positioning (crew or equipment repositioning).

business_glossary_term: Traffic Rights Category (Freedoms of the Air)
description: Classification of air traffic rights under the Freedoms of the Air framework (e.g., First Freedom, Second Freedom, Third Freedom, Fourth Freedom, Fifth Freedom, Sixth Freedom, Seventh Freedom, Eighth Freedom, Ninth Freedom). Defines the scope of international route authority.
reference: ICAO Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention)

description: Unique identifier for the hub-spoke network topology record. Primary key for the hub_spoke_topology data product.

Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Hub/spoke topology defines network structure around hub stations. Connection bank planning, MCT validation, gate sequencing, and wave optimization require direct hub station link. Role prefix 'hub_' d

Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Hub operations have distinct safety profiles (connection pressure, ground congestion, complex taxi routes). Required for hub safety performance analysis and minimum connecting time reviews. Links topo
The specific time slot (HH:MM format) allocated by the airport coordinator for this hub-spoke route at slot-constrained airports. Represents the authorized takeoff or landing time window.
Local time (HH:MM format) when the arrival wave ends for this connection bank. Marks the completion of the inbound flight cluster, after which the departure wave begins.

Local time (HH:MM format) when the arrival wave begins for this connection bank. Represents the start of the inbound flight cluster arriving at the hub to feed connecting passengers into the departure wave.

Reference to the bilateral air service agreement between countries that governs this hub-spoke route. Bilateral agreements specify traffic rights, frequencies, capacity, and designated carriers for international routes.

Boolean flag indicating whether this hub-spoke route includes codeshare agreements with partner airlines. True if codeshare partners place their flight numbers on this route, false if operated solely under the airline's own code.

Sequential identifier for the connection bank (wave) within the daily hub operation. Most hubs operate 3-6 connection banks per day, each consisting of an arrival wave followed by a departure wave to maximize connecting passenger flows.
Number of daily flights operated on this hub-spoke route pair. Used to calculate spoke thickness and assess market density.
Local time (HH:MM format) when the departure wave ends for this connection bank. Marks the completion of the outbound flight cluster for this connection bank.

Local time (HH:MM format) when the departure wave begins for this connection bank. Represents the start of the outbound flight cluster departing from the hub, carrying connecting passengers from the arrival wave.
The date when this hub-spoke topology configuration expires or is superseded by a new configuration. Null for open-ended configurations. Used to maintain historical network topology for analysis.
The date when this hub-spoke topology configuration becomes effective in the network schedule. Aligns with IATA seasonal schedule changes (typically late March and late October).

Strategic classification of the hub airport within the airline's network hierarchy. Primary hubs are the largest connecting points with the most extensive spoke networks, secondary hubs serve regional markets, focus cities offer limited connecting service, and regional hubs serve specific geographic areas.
Timestamp when this hub-spoke topology record was last modified. Used for change tracking and audit purposes in network planning systems.

The minimum time in minutes required for passengers to make a legal connection between arriving and departing flights at this hub for this specific terminal pair or connection type. MCT varies by domestic-to-domestic, domestic-to-international, international-to-international, and terminal configuration.
reference: IATA MCT Standards, Airport Authority Regulations

description: Calculated risk score (0-100) indicating the probability of passenger misconnections on this hub-spoke route based on historical OTP, MCT adequacy, connection bank timing, and operational complexity. Higher scores indicate higher misconnect risk.

Strategic priority level assigned to this hub-spoke route for network optimization initiatives. Critical routes are core to the network and receive highest investment, low priority routes may be candidates for frequency reduction or elimination.
The planned ASK capacity for this hub-spoke route, calculated as available seats multiplied by route distance in kilometers. Key metric for network capacity planning and resource allocation.

Identifier of the source planning system that created or manages this hub-spoke topology record (e.g., Jeppesen NetLine/Network, internal network planning tools). Used for data lineage and system integration.

Indicates the seasonal operating pattern for this hub-spoke route. Year-round routes operate continuously, seasonal routes operate only during specific periods (summer leisure markets, winter ski destinations), peak season routes have enhanced frequency during high-demand periods.

Boolean flag indicating whether the hub or spoke airport is slot-constrained, requiring allocated takeoff and landing slots. True for Level 3 coordinated airports (e.g., LHR, JFK, HND), false for non-coordinated airports.
Three-letter IATA airport code identifying the spoke (destination) airport connected to the hub. Represents the endpoint of a hub-spoke route segment.

Classification of the spoke route based on frequency and capacity. Thin spokes have 1-2 daily flights, thick spokes have 3+ daily flights with larger aircraft, regional spokes serve nearby markets with high frequency, ultra-thin spokes are seasonal or less-than-daily, and mega spokes are high-density trunk routes with multiple widebody flights.

The ideal time window in minutes between arrival and departure for optimal passenger connections within this connection bank. Balances MCT requirements with passenger convenience and operational efficiency. Typically 60-120 minutes for domestic connections, 90-180 minutes for international.
The target load factor (percentage of seats filled) for this hub-spoke route, used in network planning and revenue management. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 82.50 for 82.5%).

The target on-time performance percentage for this hub-spoke route, defined as flights arriving within 15 minutes of scheduled time. Used to set operational performance goals and monitor connection reliability.
reference: DOT On-Time Performance Standards, IATA Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of this hub-spoke topology record. Active topologies are in operation, planned topologies are scheduled for future implementation, suspended topologies are temporarily inactive (e.g., due to IROP or seasonal suspension), discontinued topologies have been permanently removed from the network.
Total number of flights operated per week on this hub-spoke route pair. Accounts for day-of-week variations in schedule.

Current operational status of the route: active (currently operating), suspended (temporarily halted), planned (approved but not yet launched), or discontinued (permanently ceased).

Business reason for returning the slot to the coordinator pool. Populated when slot_status is 'returned'. Common reasons include route discontinuation, schedule optimization, fleet changes, or commercial underperformance.

Indicates whether the slot allocation covers the full IATA season, a partial period within the season, or a single date. Full season slots run for the entire summer or winter season; partial season slots cover a subset of dates.

Percentage of allocated slot times that were actually used by the airline during the season. IATA WSG requires 80% usage to retain historical rights. Calculated as (flights operated within slot tolerance / total allocated slot occurrences) * 100.

Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the country or authority that issued the document. Critical for APIS reporting and visa waiver program eligibility determination.

Trusted traveller program membership number (e.g., TSA PreCheck, Global Entry, NEXUS, SENTRI, APEC Business Travel Card). Enables expedited security screening and border clearance. Stored for automatic inclusion in secure flight data.
reference: TSA Secure Flight, CBP Trusted Traveler Programs

description: Name of the trusted traveller program associated with the known traveller number. Determines which expedited lanes and services the passenger is eligible for.
Date of the most recent flight on which this document was used for travel. Helps identify stale or outdated document records and supports passenger profile analytics.

First line of the machine-readable zone at the bottom of the document. Contains document type, issuing country, and surname/given names in standardized format. Used for automated document scanning and APIS transmission.

Second line of the machine-readable zone. Contains document number, nationality, date of birth, gender, expiry date, and check digits. Enables rapid data capture via optical character recognition (OCR) at check-in kiosks and border control.
Third line of the machine-readable zone (present on some document types such as ID cards). Contains additional personal data and check digits.

Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code representing the nationality of the document holder. May differ from issuing country for dual nationals or residents. Required for APIS and visa requirement checks.
Free-text field for agent or system notes regarding the document. May include verification issues, special handling instructions, or discrepancies requiring follow-up.
City and country of birth as printed on the travel document. Required for certain APIS destinations (e.g., USA, Canada) and visa applications.

DHS Traveler Redress Inquiry Program (TRIP) control number issued to passengers who have been misidentified as a security threat. Prevents false positive watchlist matches during secure flight screening.

TSA Secure Flight screening result for USA-bound flights. Not_submitted=data not yet sent; Cleared=passenger approved for boarding; Inhibited=passenger denied boarding (no-fly list match); Conditional=requires additional screening or documentation.
reference: TSA Secure Flight Program, 49 CFR Part 1560

description: Family name or surname as printed on the travel document. Must match exactly with booking PNR (Passenger Name Record) for boarding pass issuance and border clearance.
Date and time when this document record was last modified. Tracks changes to document data, verification status, or APIS transmission results.

Current verification state of the document. Not_verified=newly entered, pending check; Verified=passed authenticity and expiry checks; Failed=document rejected (invalid format, fraudulent); Expired=document past expiry date; Flagged=requires manual review by security or compliance team.
Date and time when the document verification status was last updated. Used for audit trail and compliance reporting.
User ID or system identifier of the agent or automated process that performed the verification. Supports audit trail and accountability for document acceptance decisions.

Indicates whether a visa is required for the passengers itinerary based on nationality, destination, and transit countries. Calculated using IATA Timatic rules. If true, a separate visa document record must exist.
Unique identifier for the travel preference record. Primary key.
Reference to the passenger who owns this travel preference profile. Links to the passenger master record in Amadeus Altéa PSS.

business_glossary_term: Preferred Departure Airport Station Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Travel preferences drive booking search personalization, corporate travel policy enforcement, and loyalty program targeting by home airport. Airlines use preferred departure station to optimize route

Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: Revenue management and personalization engines use preferred route data to customize fare offers and upgrade opportunities. Loyalty programs track route preferences for targeted promotions. Critical f

Indicates whether this preference is currently active and should be applied to future bookings. Inactive preferences are retained for historical analysis but not used in operational systems.
Passenger's preferred airline alliance for travel. Influences interline and codeshare booking recommendations to maximize FFP mileage accrual and benefits.

Passenger's preferred ancillary services for automatic offer targeting: extra baggage allowance, lounge access, priority boarding, fast-track security, in-flight wifi. Supports personalized EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) generation.
Passenger's preferred format for receiving boarding passes: mobile wallet, email PDF, print-at-home, or no preference. Supports digital transformation and sustainability initiatives.

description: Passenger's preferred channel for making flight reservations. Used for channel-specific marketing and user experience optimization.
Passenger's preferred cabin class for travel. Used by revenue management for personalized offer construction and upsell targeting.
Passenger's preferred method for flight check-in. Used to send targeted reminders and optimize ground handling resource allocation.
Passenger's preferred channel for receiving airline communications (booking confirmations, flight status updates, promotional offers). Supports GDPR consent management.

Passenger's preferred connection time for multi-leg journeys: minimum (MCT only), short (MCT + 30 min), medium (1-2 hours), long (2+ hours for lounge time). Influences itinerary construction and IROP reprotection.
Timestamp when this travel preference record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

Source system that created or last updated this preference record. Used for data lineage tracking and system-of-record resolution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: altea_pss|loyalty_system|mobile_app|website|gds|call_center|import — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Indicates whether the passenger strongly prefers direct (non-stop) flights over connecting itineraries. Used for search result ranking and offer personalization.
Date from which this preference becomes active and applicable to bookings. Supports time-bound preference management (e.g., seasonal preferences, temporary dietary restrictions).
Date until which this preference remains active. Nullable for open-ended preferences. Used for automatic preference expiration and profile hygiene.
Passenger's target or preferred FFP tier level. Used for personalized upgrade offers and tier-based service customization. Links to loyalty tier status for benefit entitlement.
Indicates whether the passenger frequently travels with an infant (under 2 years). When true, bulkhead seating with bassinet availability is prioritized, and infant-specific SSRs are auto-generated.
ISO 639-1 two-letter language code for the passenger's preferred communication language. Used for personalized communications, in-flight service, and customer service interactions.
Timestamp when this travel preference record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data synchronization with Amadeus Altéa PSS.
Date when this preference was last applied to a booking or SSR generation. Used for preference relevance scoring and profile hygiene.

IATA standard 4-letter code for passenger's standing dietary meal preference (e.g., VGML=Vegetarian Vegan, KSML=Kosher, DBML=Diabetic, MOML=Muslim, AVML=Asian Vegetarian, HNML=Hindu, LCML=Low Calorie, NLML=Low Lactose, GFML=Gluten Free, BLML=Bland). This standing preference is used to auto-generate per-flight SSR meal requests.
reference: IATA Resolution 763 - Special Service Request Codes

description: Passenger's preference for the types of notifications to receive: all (flight status, booking confirmations, promotions), flight_status_only (operational updates), booking_only (transactional), none (opt-out).

Indicates whether the passenger frequently travels with pets (in-cabin or cargo). Used to auto-generate PETC (pet in cabin) or AVIH (animal in hold) SSRs and ensure compliance with pet travel regulations.
Confidence score (0.00 to 100.00) indicating the reliability of inferred preferences based on historical booking patterns and ML model predictions. Higher scores indicate stronger preference signals.
Priority ranking (1=highest) for this preference when multiple preferences of the same type exist. Used to resolve conflicts during automated SSR generation and seat assignment.
Origin of the preference data: stated (explicitly provided by passenger), inferred (derived from booking history and behavior), imported (from partner FFP or GDS profile), default (system-assigned).

Category of travel preference: seat (seating position), cabin (class of service), meal (dietary), airport (departure preference), airline (carrier preference), communication (channel preference), language (communication language). IATA 2-character airline designator code for the passenger's preferred carrier. Used for codeshare and interline booking prioritization.
Passenger's preferred location within the cabin (front, middle, rear sections, exit row for extra legroom, bulkhead for bassinet or legroom). Influences automated seat assignment logic.
Passenger's preferred seat position within the aircraft cabin. Used by Altéa PSS for automated seat assignment and SSR generation.
Passenger's preferred departure time of day. Used for personalized flight search results and schedule optimization.
Passenger's typical travel companion profile (solo traveler, family with children, business colleagues, group travel). Used for personalized service delivery and seating arrangements.

Indicates whether the passenger prefers to be automatically considered for cabin upgrades when available (using miles, revenue, or operational upgrades). Used by revenue management for upgrade inventory allocation.
Primary key for traveller_segment

Foreign key linking to loyalty.ffp_member. Business justification: Enables loyalty-driven segmentation strategy and targeted promotions. Airlines use passenger behavioral segments to design tier qualification campaigns, bonus mile offers, and retention programs—requi
Reference to the passenger being segmented. Links to the passenger master record in the passenger domain.

Foreign key linking to route.city_pair. Business justification: Segmentation models analyze route preferences by customer type (business travelers prefer hub-to-hub, leisure prefer resort destinations). Marketing campaigns target segments with city-pair-specific o
Propensity score (0.0000 to 1.0000) indicating likelihood of purchasing ancillary services (seat selection, baggage, meals, lounge access). Used for upsell targeting.
Date when the passenger was assigned to this segment. Used for segment tenure analysis and lifecycle tracking.
Preferred or most frequently used booking channel: direct web, mobile app, GDS (Global Distribution System), travel agent, call center, or mixed.
Predominant cabin class preference observed or predicted for this passenger segment: first, business, premium economy, economy, or mixed (no clear preference).
Predictive score (0.0000 to 1.0000) indicating the likelihood of passenger churn (switching to competitor or ceasing travel). Higher score indicates higher risk.
Statistical confidence or probability score (0.0000 to 1.0000) indicating the model's certainty in this segment assignment. Applicable for ML-derived segments; null for rule-based assignments.
Indicates whether the passenger is affiliated with a corporate travel program or business account (true) or is a leisure/individual traveller (false).
Timestamp when this segment assignment record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
Date from which this segment assignment becomes active and should be used for targeting, pricing, and personalization decisions.
Date until which this segment assignment remains valid. Nullable for open-ended assignments. Used for segment expiry and refresh scheduling.
Timestamp when this segment assignment record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit purposes.
Date when this segment assignment was last reviewed or refreshed by the segmentation process. Used for data quality monitoring and refresh scheduling.
Lifetime value tier classification derived from historical and predicted revenue: platinum (highest value), gold, silver, bronze, or standard. Distinct from loyalty program tier.
Level of engagement with the airline's FFP (Frequent Flyer Program): highly engaged (active accrual and redemption), engaged, moderately engaged, low engagement, or not enrolled.
Scheduled date for the next review or refresh of this segment assignment. Ensures segments remain current and accurate.
Assessed price sensitivity level of the passenger segment: very high (highly price-sensitive, seeks lowest fares), high, medium, low, or very low (price-insensitive, values convenience/service).
Estimated or actual revenue contribution value associated with this passenger segment, used for value-based segmentation and prioritization. Currency in airline's base currency.
Predominant route type preference: domestic, short-haul international, long-haul international, or mixed. Used for network planning and targeted offers.
High-level classification of the segment type: value-based, behavior-based, lifecycle stage, propensity model, demographic, or geographic segmentation.

Unique code identifying the segment type (e.g., HVT for high-value traveller, CFF for corporate frequent flyer, LSR for leisure traveller, PSN for price-sensitive, PRM for premium loyalist, LPS for lapsed traveller).
Detailed textual description of the segment characteristics, targeting criteria, and business rationale. Used for segment documentation and stakeholder communication.
Version identifier of the segmentation model or rule set used to assign this segment. Enables tracking of model evolution and reprocessing.
Human-readable name of the passenger segment (e.g., High-Value Traveller, Corporate Frequent Flyer, Leisure Traveller, Price-Sensitive, Premium Loyalist, Lapsed Traveller).
Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or context about this segment assignment. Used for manual overrides, special cases, or analyst annotations.
Numeric priority ranking (1=highest) used when a passenger belongs to multiple segments simultaneously. Determines which segment takes precedence for targeting and personalization.

Origin of the segment assignment: rules engine (business rule-based), ML model (machine learning algorithm), manual (analyst-assigned), third-party (external data provider), or hybrid (combination of methods).
Name or identifier of the system or model that generated the segment assignment (e.g., Sabre AirVision Revenue Management, internal propensity model, CRM segmentation engine).

Current lifecycle status of the segment assignment: active (in use), inactive (not currently applied), expired (past effective date), suspended (temporarily disabled), or pending (awaiting activation).

Indicates whether this segment assignment makes the passenger eligible for targeted marketing campaigns and personalized offers (true) or should be excluded (false) due to opt-out or regulatory restrictions.
Classification of passenger travel frequency based on flight count over a defined period: very high (frequent business traveller), high, medium, low, very low, or inactive (lapsed).

business_glossary_term: Advance Passenger Information System (APIS) Submission ID
description: Unique identifier for the APIS submission record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to inventory.flight_inventory. Business justification: APIS submissions are regulatory filings tied to specific flight inventory instances for border control. Customs authorities require passenger manifests linked to exact operating flights. Mandatory com
Reference to the specific flight leg for which APIS data was submitted to border control authorities.
Reference to the original APIS submission record if this is a resubmission or correction. Null for original submissions.
Reference to the passenger whose travel document data was submitted to border control authorities.

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: APIS submissions are mandated by specific border authority regulations (TSA Secure Flight, CBP APIS, EU-PNR Directive). Airlines link each submission to the governing regulatory requirement to demonst

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_violation. Business justification: Failed, late, or incomplete APIS submissions result in regulatory violations and penalties from border authorities (CBP fines up to $10,000 per violation). Airlines track which APIS failures triggered
Three-letter IATA airport code of the arrival airport for the flight leg associated with this APIS submission.
Response code returned by the border control authority indicating acceptance, rejection reason, or error condition. Codes vary by authority (e.g., CBP response codes, UKBF codes).

description: Human-readable message returned by the border control authority providing additional detail on the submission outcome or rejection reason.
reference: US CBP APIS, EU Entry/Exit System

description: Date and time when the border control authority returned a response to the APIS submission.
Code identifying the specific border control authority that received the submission (e.g., CBP for US Customs and Border Protection, UKBF for UK Border Force, EES for EU Entry/Exit System).
The specific regulatory mandate or legal requirement under which this APIS submission was made (e.g., US CBP APIS Final Rule, EU Entry/Exit System Regulation 2017/2226, ICAO Annex 9 Standard 3.47).
reference: ICAO Annex 9, US CBP APIS, EU Entry/Exit System

description: Date and time when this APIS submission record was first created in the data platform.
Three-letter IATA airport code of the departure airport for the flight leg associated with this APIS submission.
Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the destination country whose border control authority received the APIS submission.
Expiration date of the travel document as submitted to border control authorities. Snapshot at time of submission.
Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the country that issued the travel document submitted in the APIS data.
The unique document number of the travel document (passport number, national ID number, etc.) as submitted to border control authorities. Snapshot at time of submission.
Type of travel document submitted in the APIS data (passport, national ID card, visa, travel permit, refugee travel document, or other recognized travel document).
Unique reference number assigned to the APIS transmission message by the sending system or border control authority for tracking and reconciliation purposes.
Date of birth of the passenger as submitted to border control authorities. Snapshot at time of submission.
Gender of the passenger as recorded on the travel document submitted to border control authorities (M=Male, F=Female, X=Unspecified/Other). Snapshot at time of submission.
Given name(s) (first and middle names) of the passenger as they appear on the travel document submitted to border control authorities. Snapshot at time of submission.
Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code representing the nationality of the passenger as submitted to border control authorities. Snapshot at time of submission.
Surname (family name) of the passenger as it appears on the travel document submitted to border control authorities. Snapshot at time of submission.
Six-character alphanumeric Passenger Name Record locator associated with the booking for which APIS data was submitted.
Indicates whether this submission is a resubmission of previously rejected or corrected APIS data (True) or an original submission (False).
Scheduled arrival date and time of the flight leg for which APIS data was submitted.
Scheduled departure date and time of the flight leg for which APIS data was submitted.
Technical channel or interface used to transmit the APIS data (e.g., SITA Type B message, XML web service, EDI, proprietary API).

Method by which the APIS data was submitted to border control authorities: automated (system-triggered), manual (agent-initiated), batch (scheduled bulk transmission), real_time (interactive submission).
Name or code of the operational system that generated and transmitted the APIS submission (e.g., Amadeus Altéa DCS, Sabre AirCentre, SITA Horizon).

Current lifecycle status of the APIS submission: pending (awaiting authority response), accepted (approved by border control), rejected (denied by border control), error (technical transmission failure), cancelled (submission withdrawn).
reference: US CBP APIS, EU Entry/Exit System

description: Date and time when the APIS data was transmitted to the destination country border control authority. This is the principal business event timestamp for the submission.
Date and time when this APIS submission record was last modified in the data platform.
Primary key for consent

Reference to a data subject access request (DSAR), right-to-erasure request, or data portability request that triggered this consent record update. Null if the consent was not updated as part of a formal data subject request.
Reference to the passenger profile to whom this consent record belongs. Links to the authoritative passenger identity in the passenger domain.

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: Consent management must comply with GDPR Article 7, CCPA Section 1798.120, and other privacy regulations. Airlines link each consent record to the governing regulatory requirement to demonstrate lawfu
A structured log or reference to detailed audit records capturing all consent lifecycle events (granted, modified, withdrawn, expired). Supports regulatory audit and dispute resolution.
The channel or touchpoint through which the passenger provided or updated their consent. Critical for audit trail and consent validity verification.
reference: GDPR Article 7(1), EASA Consumer Protection Guidelines

description: Current lifecycle status of the consent. Indicates whether the passenger has granted, withdrawn, or is pending decision on the consent request. Expired indicates consent has passed its validity period.

The category of consent granted or withheld by the passenger. Defines the specific data processing activity for which consent is required under GDPR, CCPA, PDPA, or other applicable data protection regulations.

The date and time when this consent record was first created in the system. Recorded in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Distinct from consent_granted_timestamp, which reflects the passenger's action.
The type of device used by the passenger to provide consent. Supports user experience analysis and consent validity verification.
Boolean indicator of whether this consent record has been reviewed or flagged for review by the airline's Data Protection Officer (DPO). Used for high-risk or disputed consent cases.

The date on which the consent expires and must be re-requested from the passenger. Null for consents with no expiration. Recorded in ISO 8601 date format (yyyy-MM-dd). Required for jurisdictions with time-bound consent validity.
The date and time when the passenger granted consent. Recorded in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for GDPR and CCPA audit trails.
The IP address from which the passenger submitted their consent. Used for fraud detection, audit trail, and jurisdiction determination. May be considered PII in some jurisdictions.

The three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the legal jurisdiction under which this consent was collected. Determines applicable data protection regulation (GDPR for EU, CCPA for California, PDPA for Singapore, etc.).
reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, GDPR Territorial Scope Article 3

description: The two-letter ISO 639-1 language code in which the consent request was presented to the passenger. Required for demonstrating informed consent in the passenger's preferred language.
The date and time when this consent record was last modified. Recorded in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for audit trail and data lineage.
The lawful basis under GDPR Article 6 for processing the passenger's personal data. While this product focuses on consent, other legal bases may apply for specific processing activities.

Boolean indicator of whether this consent record pertains to a minor (passenger under the age of consent in the applicable jurisdiction). Triggers additional parental consent and verification requirements under GDPR Article 8 and COPPA.
The identifier of the system user or automated process that last modified this consent record. Supports audit trail and accountability.
Free-text field for capturing additional context, exceptions, or special handling instructions related to this consent record. Used by customer service and compliance teams.
Boolean indicator of whether the consent was obtained via opt-in (true) or opt-out (false) mechanism. GDPR requires opt-in for most marketing and profiling activities.
Boolean indicator of whether parental or guardian consent has been verified for a minor passenger. Null if minor_consent_flag is false. Required for GDPR Article 8 and COPPA compliance.

The specific purpose for which the passenger's data will be processed under this consent. Examples include marketing communications, service personalization, loyalty program analytics, or partner offers. Required for GDPR Article 13 transparency.

The date by which the airline should proactively request consent renewal from the passenger. Used for consent lifecycle management and regulatory compliance in jurisdictions requiring periodic re-consent.
The name or identifier of the source system or application that captured the consent record. Examples include Amadeus Altéa PSS, airline mobile app, loyalty portal, or third-party booking platform.
A snapshot or reference to the exact consent text presented to the passenger at the time of consent. Supports audit and dispute resolution by preserving the wording the passenger agreed to.

Description of the third-party entities or categories of entities with whom passenger data may be shared under this consent. Required for transparency under GDPR Article 13 and CCPA Section 1798.100(b).
The user agent string of the browser or application used by the passenger to provide consent. Supports technical audit and fraud detection.

The version identifier of the privacy policy or consent terms that were in effect at the time the passenger granted consent. Enables tracking of consent under different policy versions and supports re-consent workflows when policies change.

The date and time when the passenger withdrew their consent. Null if consent has not been withdrawn. Recorded in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for right-to-erasure compliance.
Primary key for data_subject_request
Identifier of the data protection officer or staff member assigned to process this data subject request.
Identifier of the passenger who submitted the data subject request. Links to the passenger master entity.
Self-referencing FK on data_subject_request (related_data_subject_request_id)
Indicates whether the data subject filed an appeal or complaint with a supervisory authority regarding the handling of their request.
Reference number assigned by the supervisory authority or internal appeals process for tracking the appeal.

Primary data protection regulation governing this request: GDPR (EU General Data Protection Regulation), CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act), LGPD (Brazilian General Data Protection Law), PIPEDA (Canadian Personal Information Protection), POPIA (South African Protection of Personal Information Act), PDPA (Singapore Personal Data Protection Act).
Date and time when the request was assigned to a data protection officer or staff member for processing.
Date and time when the data subject request was fully processed and the response was delivered to the requestor.
System timestamp when this data subject request record was first created in the database.
Comma-separated list of internal systems and databases searched to fulfill the data subject request (e.g., Amadeus Altéa PSS, loyalty system, CRM, ancillary booking system).
Regulatory deadline by which the data subject request must be fulfilled. Typically 30 days from submission under GDPR, 45 days under CCPA.
New deadline if an extension was granted. GDPR allows up to 2 additional months; CCPA allows up to 45 additional days.
Indicates whether an extension to the response deadline was granted due to complexity or volume of the request.
Justification provided to the data subject for granting an extension to the response deadline.

Method used to verify the identity of the requestor: document_upload (ID document scan), knowledge_based (security questions), biometric (fingerprint/facial recognition), email_confirmation, phone_verification, or in_person verification.
Status of identity verification process for the requestor: pending (awaiting verification), verified (identity confirmed), failed (verification unsuccessful), not_required (verification waived).
Date and time when the requestor's identity was successfully verified.
Internal working notes and comments recorded by data protection officers during the processing of the request. Not shared with the data subject.
Indicates whether the request was submitted by an authorized representative on behalf of the data subject (true) or by the data subject themselves (false).
Three-letter ISO country code representing the legal jurisdiction under which the data subject request is being processed (e.g., USA for CCPA, GBR for UK GDPR, DEU for German GDPR).
System timestamp when this data subject request record was last updated or modified.
Priority classification assigned to the data subject request based on urgency, complexity, or regulatory deadline considerations.
Total number of records or data items identified across all systems that pertain to the data subject.
Specific legal provision or regulation cited as the basis for rejecting the data subject request (e.g., GDPR Article 17(3) exception).
Detailed explanation provided to the data subject if the request was rejected, including legal basis for refusal.
Reference to the document or proof of authorization provided by the representative to act on behalf of the data subject.
Detailed description or notes provided by the requestor explaining the nature and scope of their data subject request.
Externally-visible unique reference number assigned to the data subject request for tracking and communication purposes.

Current lifecycle status of the data subject request: submitted (initial receipt), under_review (being assessed), identity_verification (verifying requestor identity), in_progress (actively being fulfilled), completed (fulfilled and closed), rejected (denied with justification), withdrawn (cancelled by requestor).

Type of data subject request: access (right to access personal data), rectification (right to correct inaccurate data), erasure (right to be forgotten), restriction (right to restrict processing), portability (right to data portability), objection (right to object to processing).
Email address of the individual submitting the data subject request for correspondence and notification purposes.
Full name of the individual submitting the data subject request. May differ from passenger name if submitted by authorized representative.
Contact phone number of the individual submitting the data subject request.
Format in which the data was provided to the data subject for access or portability requests: PDF, CSV, JSON, XML, or paper.
Method used to deliver the response to the data subject: email, postal_mail, secure_portal, in_person, or phone.
Channel through which the data subject request was submitted: web_portal, mobile_app, email, phone, postal_mail, or airport_counter.
Date and time when the data subject request was originally submitted by the passenger or their authorized representative.

business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Lawful Basis
description: The legal basis under GDPR Article 6 that justifies the processing and retention of this profile change record. Required for EU passenger data. Supports data subject access requests and regulatory audits.
The IP address of the client device or system from which the profile change was initiated. Captured for security, fraud detection, and forensic analysis. Null for backend batch processes.
reference: GDPR Article 4 (Personal Data definition), ISO 27001 security logging

description: The value of the changed field after the mutation. Stored as string representation to accommodate all data types. Null for DELETE operations. Enables forward reconstruction of profile state evolution.
reference: GDPR Article 15 (Right of Access), audit trail best practices

description: Six-character alphanumeric PNR record locator associated with the transaction that triggered the profile change. Null if the change was not initiated within the context of a specific reservation. Supports cross-domain audit trail linking.
reference: IATA PNR standards, Amadeus Altéa PSS

description: The value of the changed field immediately before the mutation. Stored as string representation to accommodate all data types. Null for INSERT operations. Supports point-in-time reconstruction and rollback scenarios.
reference: GDPR Article 15 (Right of Access), audit trail best practices

description: Cryptographic hash (SHA-256) of the complete change record payload. Ensures immutability and tamper detection for audit integrity. Supports forensic verification and regulatory compliance with audit trail non-repudiation requirements.

The date on which this audit record is eligible for deletion or archival per the airlines data retention policy and applicable regulatory requirements. Null for records with indefinite retention. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: GDPR Article 5 (Storage Limitation), internal data retention policy

description: Boolean indicator of whether this history record represents a reversal or rollback of a previous change. True if this is a corrective reversal, False for normal forward changes. Supports error correction audit trails.

Unique identifier of the user session or API session during which the profile change occurred. Enables correlation of multiple changes within a single interaction and supports session replay for troubleshooting.

Unique identifier linking this profile change to the broader business transaction or session that triggered it. Enables correlation of profile mutations with reservation bookings, check-in events, or loyalty transactions.

The HTTP user agent string identifying the browser, mobile app version, or API client that submitted the profile change. Supports device analytics, compatibility troubleshooting, and fraud pattern detection.
Primary key for watchlist_check
Employee or agent identifier of the security officer who resolved the watchlist match.
Reference to the passenger profile being screened.

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: Watchlist screening is mandated by TSA Secure Flight (49 CFR 1560), EU-PNR Directive, and national security regulations. Airlines link each screening event to the governing requirement to demonstrate

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_violation. Business justification: Screening failures (false negatives, missed checks, system outages) can result in regulatory violations and enforcement actions from TSA or border authorities. Airlines track which watchlist check fai

business_glossary_term: Advance Passenger Information (API) / Passenger Name Record (PNR) Indicator
description: Indicates whether the screening was performed using API data, PNR data, or both.
Indicates whether a boarding pass was issued following the watchlist check clearance.
Current status of the watchlist check record in its lifecycle.
Date and time when the watchlist screening check was performed.
Date and time when this watchlist check record was first created in the system.
Date when this watchlist check record must be purged per regulatory data retention requirements.
Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight destination.
Date and time when the watchlist check result expires and a new check must be performed.
Flight number for which the watchlist check was performed, following IATA flight number format.
TSA PreCheck or other trusted traveler program number that may expedite screening clearance.
reference: TSA PreCheck Program, CBP Global Entry

description: Description of the reason for the match, including which passenger attributes triggered the screening alert.
Numerical confidence score (0.00 to 100.00) indicating the likelihood of a true match when a potential match is detected.
Result of the watchlist screening check indicating whether the passenger matched any watchlist entries.
reference: TSA Secure Flight Program, DHS Traveler Redress Inquiry Program (TRIP)

description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight origin.
Six-character alphanumeric PNR locator code associated with the booking being screened.
DHS Traveler Redress Inquiry Program (TRIP) redress number provided by the passenger to prevent false matches.
Reference number or identifier for the regulatory submission of screening results to TSA, EU authorities, or other governing bodies.
reference: TSA Secure Flight Program, EU PNR Directive 2016/681

description: Action taken to resolve a potential or confirmed match, including clearance, escalation, or denial.
reference: TSA Secure Flight Program, DHS TRIP

description: Free-text notes documenting the resolution process, verification steps, and outcome.
Date and time when the watchlist match was resolved or cleared.
Scheduled departure date of the flight for which the passenger was screened.
Two or three-letter country or region code indicating the regulatory jurisdiction under which screening was performed.
The regulatory or security program under which the watchlist check was performed.
reference: TSA Secure Flight Program, OFAC Sanctions Programs, Interpol Notices, EU PNR Directive 2016/681

description: Name or identifier of the automated screening system that performed the watchlist check.
Version number of the screening algorithm or watchlist data used for the check.
Indicates whether the passenger was designated for enhanced secondary screening (SSSS - Secondary Security Screening Selection).
Date and time when screening results were submitted to the regulatory authority.
reference: TSA Secure Flight Program, EU PNR Directive 2016/681

description: Date and time when this watchlist check record was last modified.
Name or identifier of the specific watchlist that triggered a match (e.g., No Fly List, Selectee List, OFAC SDN List).
reference: TSA Secure Flight, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List

description: Primary key for passenger_booking
Unique identifier for this passenger-flight booking record. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to the specific flight-date inventory record for this booking
Foreign key linking to the passenger profile who holds this booking
Reference to the PNR that contains this booking. Multiple bookings (multi-leg journeys) can belong to the same PNR.
Number of checked baggage pieces allowed for this booking based on fare class and route.
Total checked baggage weight allowance in kilograms for this booking.
Date and time when the passenger's boarding pass was scanned at the gate and the passenger boarded the aircraft. Null if not yet boarded.
Single-letter fare class (booking class) code for this reservation (e.g., Y, B, M for economy; J, C for business; F, A for first). Determines fare rules, upgrade eligibility, and mileage accrual.
Channel through which this booking was created (direct web, mobile app, GDS, call center, airport counter, travel agent, corporate booking tool).

Current lifecycle status of this booking. CONFIRMED=seat confirmed, WAITLISTED=on waitlist, CANCELLED=booking cancelled, NO_SHOW=passenger did not board, CHECKED_IN=passenger checked in, BOARDED=passenger boarded aircraft.
Physical cabin class for this booking (FIRST, BUSINESS, PREMIUM_ECONOMY, ECONOMY). Determines service level and seat location.
Date and time when the passenger checked in for this flight (online, mobile, kiosk, or airport counter). Null if not yet checked in.
Date and time when this booking was originally created in the reservation system.
Base fare amount paid for this booking in the transaction currency, excluding taxes and fees.
Detailed fare basis code that encodes fare rules, restrictions, seasonality, and pricing logic for this booking (e.g., YRT14, BAPX21).
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the fare amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
Frequent flyer program number provided for this booking to accrue miles and status credits. May differ from passenger profile FFP if using partner program.
Assigned seat number for this passenger on this flight (e.g., 12A, 34F). Null if seat not yet assigned.
Comma-separated list of IATA SSR codes for this booking (e.g., WCHR for wheelchair, VGML for vegetarian meal, PETC for pet in cabin).
13-digit IATA e-ticket number issued for this booking (airline code + ticket number). Unique identifier for the ticketed reservation.
Date and time when this booking was last modified (seat change, status change, upgrade, etc.).
Flag indicating whether this booking was upgraded from the original booking class (e.g., operational upgrade, loyalty upgrade, paid upgrade).
Primary key for passenger_booking_passenger
Unique identifier for this booking-passenger link record. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to the passenger profile participating in this booking
Foreign key linking to the PNR that contains this passenger
Date and time when this passenger boarded the aircraft for this booking. Null if not yet boarded. Identified in detection phase.
Date and time when this passenger was added to the PNR. May differ from PNR creation timestamp if passengers added incrementally. Identified in detection phase.

Role of this passenger within the booking context. PRIMARY=main contact/booker, COMPANION=traveling with primary, INFANT=lap infant associated with adult, UNACCOMPANIED_MINOR=child traveling alone with special handling. Identified in detection phase.
Date and time when this passenger was removed or cancelled from this PNR. Null if passenger remains active in booking. Identified in detection phase.
Date and time when this passenger checked in for this specific booking. Null if not yet checked in. Identified in detection phase.
Meal type preference for this passenger in this specific booking using IATA SSR meal codes. May override profile-level preference. Identified in detection phase.

Indicates how the passenger name in this booking relates to the profile name. EXACT_MATCH=identical, VARIANT=minor spelling differences, ALIAS=known alternate name. Used for profile matching and fraud detection. Identified in detection phase.
Position of this passenger within the PNR passenger list. Used for ordering passengers in booking displays and documents. Identified in detection phase.
Seat location preference for this passenger in this specific booking. May override profile-level preference. Identified in detection phase.
Primary key for passenger_promotion_enrollment
Foreign key to loyalty.loyalty_promotion.loyalty_promotion_id
Foreign key linking to the passenger profile who enrolled in the promotion
Unique identifier for this promotion enrollment record. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to the loyalty promotion campaign
Total bonus miles earned by this passenger under this specific promotion. Accumulated as qualifying activities occur. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

Channel through which the passenger enrolled in the promotion: web, mobile_app, email_link, auto_enrolled (system-initiated for eligible members), call_center, partner_site. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Timestamp when this enrollment record was first created in the system. Immutable audit field.
Date when the passenger enrolled in or was automatically registered for this promotion. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

Current status of the enrollment: enrolled (active, tracking progress), qualified (met all requirements), disqualified (violated terms), expired (promotion ended before qualification), withdrawn (member opted out). Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Timestamp when this enrollment record was last modified. Updated when status changes or bonus miles are awarded.

Percentage progress (0.00 to 100.00) toward meeting the promotion qualification requirements. Calculated based on flights taken, miles earned, or other promotion-specific criteria. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Primary key for pnr_link

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Booking agents create/modify PNRs; essential for commission calculation, quality audits, fraud investigation, regulatory accountability (IATA agent tracking), and performance management. Standard airl

Foreign key linking to loyalty.ffp_member. Business justification: Resolves PNR-level frequent flyer number to loyalty account for automated mile accrual and upgrade processing. Airlines must link each PNR passenger to loyalty profile for post-flight accrual batch jo

Foreign key linking to inventory.flight_inventory. Business justification: PNR passenger associations must link to specific flight inventory for seat control, load management, and overbooking decisions. Revenue management and departure control systems require this for real-t

Foreign key linking to reservation.pnr. Business justification: pnr_link currently stores pnr_locator as string; adding FK to reservation.pnr enables customer service agents to reconcile passenger profile history with booking records during dispute resolution, ref
Foreign key reference to the passenger profile in the passenger domain. Identifies the individual traveler whose identity is linked to the PNR.

Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: IROP (irregular operations) systems use PNR-route linkage for automated rebooking and disruption management. Route-level tracking enables journey analytics and end-to-end customer experience measureme

business_glossary_term: Advance Passenger Information (API) Data Submitted Flag
description: Boolean flag indicating whether Advance Passenger Information (passport, visa, destination address) has been submitted to authorities for this passenger on this PNR. True if submitted; false if not yet submitted. Required for international travel compliance.

business_glossary_term: Advance Passenger Information System (APIS) Submission Timestamp
description: Date and time when API data was transmitted to border control authorities for this passenger. Null if not yet submitted. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Date and time when this passenger boarded the aircraft for the flight(s) on this PNR. Null if not yet boarded. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Date and time when this passenger was first linked to the PNR in the reservation system. Represents the initial association event. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Defines the passenger's role within the PNR booking. Lead passenger is the primary contact and decision-maker; accompanying passenger travels with the lead; infant is a child under 2; group leader manages a group booking; group member is part of a group.

Standardized code indicating the reason for cancellation of this passenger-PNR link. Passenger_request indicates voluntary cancellation; schedule_change indicates airline-initiated change; involuntary indicates denied boarding or operational reasons; no_show indicates passenger did not appear; duplicate indicates duplicate booking; fraud indicates suspected fraudulent booking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: passenger_request|schedule_change|involuntary|no_show|duplicate|fraud|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Date and time when this passenger-PNR link was cancelled. Null if link is still active or completed. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Date and time when this passenger checked in for the flight(s) on this PNR. Null if not yet checked in. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Email address provided for this passenger on this PNR for booking-specific communications. May differ from the email stored in the passenger profile if the passenger provided a different contact for this booking.

Phone number provided for this passenger on this PNR for booking-specific communications. May differ from the phone stored in the passenger profile if the passenger provided a different contact for this booking.
Name of the emergency contact person for this passenger on this PNR. Used in case of travel disruption or incident.
Phone number of the emergency contact person for this passenger on this PNR. Used in case of travel disruption or incident.
Boolean flag indicating whether this passenger-PNR link is part of a group booking (typically 10 or more passengers traveling together). True if group booking; false if individual or small party.
Name of the group if this is a group booking. Examples: corporate event name, tour group name, sports team name. Null for non-group bookings.
Boolean flag indicating whether this passenger is an infant (under 2 years old) traveling on this PNR. True if infant; false otherwise. Affects pricing, seating, and service requirements.
Boolean flag indicating whether the infant is traveling on an adult's lap without a separate seat. True if on lap; false if infant has own seat. Impacts seat assignment and safety procedures.
TSA PreCheck, Global Entry, or other trusted traveler program number. Enables expedited security screening. Applicable primarily for US travel.
reference: US Transportation Security Administration (TSA) PreCheck Program

description: Date and time of the most recent modification to this passenger-PNR link record. Includes changes to name, SSRs, status, or any other attribute. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Current lifecycle status of the passenger-PNR association. Active indicates valid link; cancelled indicates booking was cancelled; no_show indicates passenger did not appear for travel; checked_in indicates passenger has checked in; boarded indicates passenger has boarded; completed indicates travel is finished; suspended indicates temporary hold. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|cancelled|no_show|checked_in|boarded|completed|suspended — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Passenger's meal preference for this PNR, typically expressed as a four-letter SSR code (e.g., VGML for vegetarian, KSML for kosher, MOML for Muslim meal). Used for catering planning.

Categorizes the type of passenger association within the PNR. Primary indicates the main traveler; infant_on_lap indicates a child under 2 traveling on an adult's lap without a separate seat; group_member indicates part of a group booking; accompanying indicates a passenger traveling with another; unaccompanied_minor indicates a child traveling alone; crew_deadhead indicates crew repositioning without duty.

Boolean flag indicating whether the PNR passenger name differs from the legal name on the passenger profile. True if mismatch detected; false if names match. Used for data quality monitoring and potential identity verification issues.
Sequential position of this passenger within the PNR. Used to maintain passenger order in multi-passenger bookings and for referencing specific passengers in PNR transactions.

Six-character alphanumeric booking reference code that uniquely identifies the PNR in the reservation system. This is the primary business identifier used by agents, passengers, and partner systems to retrieve the booking.

Passenger name exactly as it appears on the PNR booking. May differ from the legal name stored in the passenger profile due to name changes, spelling variations, or data entry differences. Used for ticket issuance and travel document verification.

Department of Homeland Security Traveler Redress Inquiry Program (DHS TRIP) number for passengers who have been misidentified in the past. Used to prevent false matches with watch lists. Applicable primarily for US travel.
reference: US Transportation Security Administration (TSA) Secure Flight Program

description: Passenger's preferred seat location for this PNR. Window, aisle, or middle seat preference. Used for seat assignment optimization.

Identifies the Global Distribution System or booking channel that created the PNR association. Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport are major GDS platforms; direct indicates airline's own PSS; other values indicate distribution channels. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: amadeus|sabre|travelport|direct|travel_agent|online|mobile|call_center|airport — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Name of the Passenger Service System that originated this PNR link record. Examples include Amadeus Altéa, Sabre SabreSonic, or proprietary airline PSS platforms. Enables traceability to the system of record.

Comma-separated list of four-letter SSR codes requested for this passenger on this PNR. Examples: WCHR (wheelchair), VGML (vegetarian meal), PETC (pet in cabin), UMNR (unaccompanied minor). Captures service requirements specific to this booking.
Thirteen-digit electronic ticket number issued for this passenger on this PNR. Format: 3-digit airline code + 10-digit serial number. Links the passenger-PNR association to the ticketing domain.
Expiration date of the travel document provided for this passenger on this PNR. Used to validate document validity for travel dates. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
Three-letter ISO country code of the country that issued the travel document. Used for border control and visa requirement determination.

Passport or other travel document number provided for this passenger on this PNR. Used for international travel verification and API submission. May differ from the document stored in the passenger profile if the passenger used a different document for this booking.
reference: ICAO Doc 9303 - Machine Readable Travel Documents

description: Type of travel document provided for this passenger on this PNR. Passport is most common for international travel; national_id may be accepted for regional travel; visa indicates entry authorization; refugee_travel_document for refugees.
Unique identifier for the SSR record instance. Primary key.

Identifier of the booking agent, customer service representative, or system user who created this SSR record.
reference: Amadeus Altéa PSS User Management Module

Reference to the specific flight leg for which this SSR applies. Nullable if SSR applies to entire journey.
reference: Amadeus Altéa PSS Flight Inventory Module

description: Foreign key linking to crew.crew_member. Business justification: Airlines track which cabin crew member fulfilled special service requests (wheelchair assistance, medical needs, special meals) for quality assurance, training feedback, and incident investigation. Op
Reference to the passenger profile to whom this SSR is linked.
reference: Amadeus Altéa PSS Passenger Profile Module

description: Reference to the PNR booking under which this SSR was requested.

Foreign key linking to revenue.emd. Business justification: SSRs (special service requests like meals, wheelchairs, extra baggage) are sold as ancillary services and documented via EMDs. Links service delivery records to revenue recognition for ancillary billi

Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: SSR fulfillment planning requires route-level context (wheelchair assistance varies by airport infrastructure, meal catering by route length/type). Operations teams pre-position resources by route. Co

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Special service requests (wheelchairs, medical oxygen, special meals, unaccompanied minor escort) are fulfilled by contracted vendors tracked in procurement. Airlines must link SSR fulfillment to vend
Minimum number of hours before departure that this SSR must be requested. Nullable if no advance notice required.
reference: IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions Manual (PSCRM)

Date and time when the SSR was cancelled. Nullable if not cancelled.
Monetary amount charged for this SSR service. Nullable if not chargeable or charge not yet determined.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the SSR charge amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
Date and time when the SSR was confirmed by the airline or service provider. Nullable if not yet confirmed.
System timestamp when this SSR record was first created in the database.
Description of special equipment needed to fulfill this SSR (e.g., onboard wheelchair, oxygen concentrator, stretcher, incubator).
Free-text notes recorded by ground staff or cabin crew documenting how the SSR was fulfilled, any issues encountered, or passenger feedback.
Operational instructions for ground staff, cabin crew, or service providers on how to fulfill this SSR, including equipment needs, timing, and coordination requirements.
Boolean flag indicating whether this SSR incurs a charge to the passenger (true) or is provided as a complimentary service (false).
Boolean flag indicating whether this SSR applies to an interline segment operated by a partner carrier (true) or an own-metal flight (false).
Boolean flag indicating whether this SSR was auto-populated from the passenger's standing travel preferences (true) or requested ad-hoc for this booking (false).
reference: Amadeus Altéa PSS Passenger Profile Module

description: Four-letter IATA meal code for dietary SSRs (e.g., VGML for vegetarian, KSML for kosher, DBML for diabetic). Applicable only when ssr_code is SPML.
Status of medical clearance for SSRs requiring medical approval. Values: not_required, pending, approved, denied.
Two-character IATA airline code of the carrier operating the flight for which this SSR applies. Relevant for interline SSRs.
Date and time when the SSR was initially requested by the passenger or booking agent.
Boolean flag indicating whether this SSR type requires advance notice to the airline (true) or can be requested at check-in or boarding (false).
reference: IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions Manual (PSCRM)

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this SSR requires medical clearance or MEDA form approval before confirmation (true for MEDA, OXYG, STCR SSRs).
Date and time when the SSR service was actually delivered or completed. Nullable if not yet delivered.

High-level categorization of the SSR type for reporting and operational grouping (accessibility, medical, dietary, unaccompanied minor, pet transport, special baggage, other). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: accessibility|medical|dietary|unaccompanied_minor|pet_transport|special_baggage|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions Manual (PSCRM)

description: Four-letter IATA SSR code identifying the type of service requested (e.g., WCHR, WCHC, BLND, DEAF, MEDA, OXYG, SPML, UMNR, PETC, DPNA).
Free-text description providing additional details about the SSR, including handling instructions, meal preferences, medical conditions, or special equipment requirements.
reference: IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions Manual (PSCRM)

description: Current lifecycle status of the SSR indicating whether the service has been requested, confirmed by the airline, waitlisted, cancelled, denied, or completed.
System timestamp when this SSR record was last modified.
Specific wheelchair assistance level for accessibility SSRs: WCHR (can walk stairs), WCHS (cannot walk stairs), WCHC (immobile, requires onboard wheelchair). Applicable only for wheelchair SSR codes.
reference: IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions Manual (PSCRM) - Accessibility Services

Foreign key linking to the route master record
Average fare amount paid by this passenger for this route across all historical bookings. Used for price sensitivity analysis and personalized pricing strategies.
Timestamp when this travel history record was first created in the system.
Date of the passenger's first travel on this route. Used for customer tenure analysis and lifecycle marketing.
Timestamp when this travel history record was last updated.
Most recent date when this passenger traveled on this route. Used for recency analysis in customer segmentation and reactivation campaigns.
Most frequently booked cabin class by this passenger on this route. Values: economy, premium_economy, business, first. Used for targeted upgrade offers and cabin-specific promotions.

Calculated score (0.00 to 100.00) representing the strength of this passenger's preference for this route based on frequency, recency, fare paid, and booking behavior. Used for route-specific marketing and personalization.
Total number of bookings made by this passenger for this route, including no-shows and cancellations. Differs from travel_frequency which counts completed trips only.
Total number of times this passenger has traveled on this specific route. Used for route affinity scoring and frequent traveler identification.
Unique identifier for the group booking record. Primary key for coordinated reservations of 10+ passengers travelling together under a single group contract.
Identifier of the airline sales representative or agent responsible for managing the group booking relationship and contract execution.
IATA office identifier or internal office code where the group booking was created and is managed. Supports organizational accountability and reporting.
Service class or cabin category contracted for the group booking. Defines the level of service and amenities provided to group passengers.
Free-text explanation or coded reason for group booking cancellation. Supports operational analysis and customer service documentation.
Date and time when the group booking was cancelled. Null if the booking has not been cancelled. Critical for refund and penalty processing.
Unique contract reference number assigned to the group booking agreement. Used for legal documentation and financial settlement tracking.
Date and time when the group booking record was initially created in the reservation system. Audit trail for booking lifecycle tracking.
Scheduled departure date for the outbound travel segment of the group booking. Primary travel date for group coordination and planning.
Initial deposit amount required to secure the group booking. Represents the upfront payment obligation per the group contract terms.
Deadline by which the deposit payment must be received to maintain the group booking option or confirmation status.
Indicator of whether the required deposit payment has been received and processed. True indicates deposit obligation fulfilled.
Three-letter IATA airport code representing the primary arrival point for the group travel. Defines the ending location of the group itinerary.
Negotiated fare basis code applicable to the group booking. Defines the fare rules, restrictions, and conditions governing the group travel contract.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the negotiated fare amount. Defines the currency in which group pricing is denominated.
Deadline by which full payment for all confirmed seats must be received. Critical milestone for group booking financial settlement.
Current lifecycle status of the group booking indicating progression through reservation, confirmation, ticketing, and fulfillment stages.
Primary email address of the group coordinator for all booking communications, updates, and documentation delivery.

description: Full name of the primary contact person responsible for coordinating the group booking on behalf of the organizing entity.

description: Primary contact phone number for the group coordinator. Used for urgent communications and operational coordination.
reference: GDPR Article 4, IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions

description: Business or descriptive name assigned to the group booking for identification and reference purposes.
